items.summary: RIL's consolidated revenue rose 27. 8% year-on-year to ₹3. 6 lakh crore in the September quarter, with Ebitda of ₹62,409 crore at a record high but up only 23. 9%. The O2C business led growth, pushing Ebitda 67. 9% to ₹25,203 crore and nearly 40% of group total. Retail Ebitda fell 10. 2% to ₹6,120 crore amid margin pressure from digital commerce investments and input costs. Jio Platforms reported double-digit revenue and profit growth after its October listing, with customer base rising 7. 1% to 542. 4 million and 5G users reaching 55. 3%.
items.title: Reliance eyes growth from O2C, retail and Jio businesses

items.summary: Asian share markets fell Monday amid fears over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and high oil prices limiting bond appeal. Concerns about corporate default insurance costs rose, while gold hit a one-year low. The week's focus is on earnings from Apple, AMD and Palantir after Intel dropped nearly 29 per cent Friday. Goldman Sachs analysts expect hyperscaler capex to reach $800 billion this year, with S&P 500 EPS growth of about 30 per cent in 2026.
items.title: Asian shares slip as AI spending worries weigh on tech ahead of Apple earnings

items.summary: Hong Kong is considering new rules targeting asset-intensive reinsurance, one of the fastest-growing segments of its insurance market, according to people familiar with the matter. The Hong Kong Insurance Authority has sought industry feedback on changes that would require insurers to either notify or seek approval depending on circumstances such as credit ratings and materiality. A revised guideline is expected to take effect in 2027, the regulator said. Representatives for several firms declined to comment.
items.title: Hong Kong Considers Rules for Asset-Intensive Reinsurance

items.summary: Kranthi Bathini of WealthMills Securities said festive activity extending into November, stronger corporate earnings and renewed foreign buying could support Indian equities. He noted October gains in the Sensex (1.9%) and Nifty (2.7%), while mid- and small-cap indices fell 4% and 6.3%. Global uncertainties and high oil prices remain key risks. Aditya Agarwala of InvestValue Capital advised favouring companies with strong domestic earnings visibility and pricing power.
items.title: Indian equity strategist sees November tailwinds amid macro risks

items.summary: The Supreme Court upheld a Delhi High Court order permitting the Income Tax Department to reassess Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, sons of former Chief Justice YK Sabharwal. The bench affirmed that a March 31, 2015 notice under Section 148 was validly issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10 regarding share sale deals worth Rs 255 crore.
items.title: Supreme Court Upholds Tax Reassessment of Ex-CJI's Sons' Share Sales

items.summary:
The Ukrainian Air Force says its air raid alert app was hacked on Sunday and briefly warned Kyiv of a radiation threat. The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said it was an app failure, while Russian authorities later blamed the hack. A partisan group called Atesh reportedly claimed responsibility for fake nuclear warnings inside Russia. Officials urged people to rely on official sources as false alerts spread nationwide before all-clear messages followed.

visual null},
items.title: Ukraine's Air Force Says Its Raid App Was Hacked With False Threats

items.summary: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets after the exchange reopened on Sunday following what is called the largest hack in history, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. The FBI and other organisations have accused North Korea's Lazarus Group (aka TraderTraitor) of responsibility. Binance says it has covered around 95% of stolen assets using treasury, futures insurance and emergency reserve funds, while reserving more than $6.34bn for the fallout; remaining recovery may take longer.
items.title: Binance Reopens After Record Hack as Customers Withdraw $3.6bn

items.summary: Donald Trump attacked Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at an Iowa campaign event, repeatedly calling him a “jihadist” and saying Congress would need a special metal detector if he won. The comments targeted a tight Michigan race ahead of Tuesday’s midterms. El-Sayed responded to his ally Hayley Stevens after she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers.
items.title: Trump Attacks El-Sayed at Iowa Rally

items.summary: The administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is considering a registration system for foreign agents as part of planned antiespionage legislation. Under the expected rules, individuals and organizations collecting information or running influence operations on behalf of foreign governments would be required to register so their activities become visible. The government plans to submit related legislation to the Diet as early as next spring after an expert panel presented a concrete plan last week.
items.title: Japan Weighs Foreign Agent Registration in Antiespionage Law

items.summary: Ukraine's air force said on Sunday it suspected the country's nationwide Air Alarm application had probably been subjected to hostile interference, warning that threat notifications no longer reflected reality. The announcement came minutes after a local Kherson ceasefire ended and followed warnings from Ukraine's Centre for Countering Disinformation about mismatched information.
items.title: Ukraine's air force says nationwide alert app likely hacked after ceasefire ends

items.summary: Mass demonstrations in Germany that passed largely peacefully on Saturday erupted in violence at nightfall, with rioters facing off against police across Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin. Authorities blocked Die Zeil in Frankfurt after demonstrators smashed shop windows and stole goods, arresting more than 30 people. Officers also arrested one person suspected of breaking into a gun store.
items.title: German Protests Turn Violent as Activists Clash with Police

items.summary: Supermodel Heidi Klum wore a gruesome severed-hand costume at her annual New York Halloween party on Oct 31, marking the event's 25th year. Only her eyes and mouth showed as blood dripped from her tongue. She said it took about five to six hours to get into the costume but making it took longer.
items.title: Heidi Klum Reveals Giant Hand Halloween Costume

items.summary: Finshots asks whether China's AI boom has already collapsed while the US still bets on it. It reports that over four months China's STAR 50 index fell 40%, wiping out nearly $480 billion in investor wealth, and describes how state-backed money drove retail traders into a speculative frenzy where AI stocks reached 42% of market value and 57% of trading volume. The piece frames the crash as part of a global reset, noting Nvidia shed $600 billion in one day after DeepSeek's low-cost model, while Alphabet lost nearly $500 billion this week. It draws an analogy to dark fibre from the dot-com era but cautions that AI chips may lose value faster than cables did, leaving companies still needing to make trillions pay off.
items.title: China's AI bubble bursts first as stocks crash

items.summary: A Learjet crashed into a South Florida neighborhood, killing nine people aboard the aircraft bound from Austin to the Bahamas. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it came down near Cresthaven at 12:50 pm. The crash occurred less than seven miles from Mar-a-Lago and triggered a large fireball. FAA officials are sending a team to support an NTSB investigation, which is planned for Monday.
items.title: Learjet Crash Kills Nine Near Mar-a-Lago in Florida

items.summary: Delhi-NCR recorded an air quality index of 244 on October 21, the worst in 100 days, marking the start of a worsening pollution season. Gufran Beig and Prarthana Borah explain that El Niño could enhance weather trapping by reducing wind speeds further and weakening western disturbances, keeping pollutants suspended longer. CEEW's study found higher very poor and severe AQI days during an El Niño year (2023-’24) versus La Nina years. Experts caution that more long-term research is needed to isolate meteorological impacts from pollution sources, urging proactive mitigation of vehicular, industrial and crop-residue emissions.
items.title: El Niño May Intensify Delhi Winter Pollution Haze

items.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) welcomed the GST Council's reforms, which remove arrest powers and raise the prosecution threshold fivefold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee called it a landmark move toward trust-based governance that keeps penalties for serious violations while improving enforcement precision and reducing business uncertainty.
items.title: CII Praises GST Council Decriminalisation Reforms as Trust-Based Shift

items.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd clarified that an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered against founder Subhash Chandra in his personal capacity carries no bearing on the company. The probe, led by the Central Bureau of Investigation after a first information report from LIC Housing Finance Ltd, alleges fraud causing public sector loss exceeding ₹1,322 crore over two credit facilities totaling ₹980 crore sanctioned in 2018.
items.title: Zee Separates Founder Probe From Corporate Operations

items.summary: Democratic party leaders failed to prevent a schism in Michigan's must-win Senate race, where Rep. Haley Stevens surprised colleagues by endorsing Republican nominee Mike Rogers after previously vowing to back Abdul El-Sayed. The defection drew praise from President Trump and calls for her removal from the House Democratic Caucus. Raskin called himself 'dumbfounded,' while Schumer labeled it a 'despicable betrayal.' Analysts see deep divides over Israel and party-left relations, with tensions likely extending into 2028.
items.title: Michigan Democrats Fracture Over Stevens' Rogers Endorsement

items.summary: Oilprice.com reports that samarium sells for as much as 346 times more in North America than in China, framing the gap as a preview of prices if Beijing curtails exports. The piece centers on REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), which it says is positioning to profit from one of the most serious shortages developing in America's rare earth supply chain. It notes that jet engines, EVs and wind turbines depend on magnets made with these metals, yet U.S. manufacturers still buy at Chinese prices; American firms purchase about 48,000 tonnes of magnet feedstock yearly while domestic output reached just 300 tonnes in 2025. The article attributes a metallization blind spot to Canaccord Genuity and cites REalloys' own claims that it holds the only operating heavy rare earth metallization capability in North America and reported $122.4 million in cash at end of June, with expansions fully funded. It flags an ownership conflict: Oilprice.com's owner holds shares or options in REalloys. The piece also surveys copper and lithium producers expanding into critical minerals but does not independently verify any company statement.
items.title: REalloys Bets on Rare-Earth Metallization Shortage

items.summary: Some investors are lowering expectations for US economic growth as red flags emerged over the sustainability of the country's rapid AI buildout. The tech-heavy Nasdaq slid into correction territory on Friday after investors unwound their AI bets, with Intel stock plunging 29% and S&P Global revising Meta's outlook to 'negative.' A strategist told Bloomberg that earnings misses are raising sober questions about AI investments.
items.title: Investors Trim US Growth Expectations After Weak AI Earnings

items.summary: AI-related fears over corporate cash flow and spending scale pushed default-insurance costs higher last week, while gold fell to a one-year low amid margin-call selling. Asian equities edged lower: the Nikkei dropped 0.5%, South Korea's index lost 0.8% after shedding 16% in October, and MSCI's Asia-Pacific outside Japan index eased 0.4%. The week's focus shifts to earnings from Apple, AMD and Palantir following Intel's near-29% fall. Futures imply a 72% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise, with only 55 basis points of tightening priced in versus more than 70 last month.
items.title: Asian shares slip as AI capex worries and Apple earnings loom

items.summary: Five of China's largest state-owned banks reported their fastest quarterly profit growth since 2021 or 2022, with gains between 6% and 11%, driven by stabilising net interest margins and steadier asset quality despite a slowing economy. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China posted 10% year-on-year net profit growth in the third quarter, while Agricultural Bank of China, China Construction Bank and Bank of Communications reported rates of 10.8%, 9.8% and 10.1%. Bank of China grew more slowly at 6.4% amid trade tensions. Analysts note that benefits from deposit repricing are fading but monetary easing supports margins, while rising bond gains add volatility as banks expand into chip sector investments.
items.title: China's Big Banks Report Fastest Quarterly Profit Growth in Years

items.summary: Ritesh Jain of Pinetree Macro says large-cap banks and IT stocks are seen as an anti-AI trade, drawing model-driven rather than broad foreign inflows. He notes a shift in global investment flows amid signs of deflation in the AI trade. BlackRock remains strategically overweight India, closely watching recent inflow pace after earlier outflows.
items.title: Foreign investors return to Indian markets as AI-trade optimism shifts global flows

items.summary: On Sunday, Sikh riot survivors and organisations questioned Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, marking the 42nd anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings. The protest drew BJP leaders who saw political opportunity ahead of Punjab assembly elections due in 2027, framing the timing as ammunition against Congress.
items.title: Sikh Groups Question Timing of INDIA Bloc Rally on Massacre Anniversary

items.summary: Authorities said four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed last week in a high-speed collision outside Urda. A legal body of police and forensics experts announced on Sunday the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims; all but three are now identified, with three missing-person reports still active for two Australians and one Japanese citizen.
items.title: Foreign nationals among dead in Spain train crash

items.summary: Democratic candidates lead in polls ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, with the party projected to clear 218 seats needed to flip the House and tie or edge key Senate races. The article notes recent polling misses—Trump outperforming predictions in 2016 and 2024, a Michigan primary that swung from predicted double-digit margins to just 1%, and Wisconsin's governor race flipping by less than a percent—to question accuracy. Clifford Young of Ipsos Public Affairs attributes challenges to declining landline reach and lower participation among conservatives. He cautions against overreading the data, noting polls can err both ways and that historical midterm patterns often favor the party out of power.
items.title: Polls Favor Democrats in Midterms Despite Past Polling Misses

items.summary: A submission to Victoria's construction royal commission, first reported by The Age, alleges the state government inflated costs and threatened a senior public servant into supporting its preferred Airport Rail Link route through Sunshine. An anonymous former planning expert reportedly said between $3.8 billion and $4.6 billion of unnecessary tunnelling was added to an alternate Maribyrnong route to make it less attractive than the Sunshine option, which totals up to $4.6 billion in additions. The government declined to comment, saying it would let the royal commission finish its work. Shadow Minister Evan Mulholland called the conduct bullying and intimidation, while minister Jaclyn Symes questioned the claims' sources. Centre for Public Integrity's William Partlett said the allegations may signal more to come.
items.title: Victorian Labor Alleged of Pressuring Officials Over Rail Route

items.summary: The Tasmanian Electoral Commission has finalised the Hobart City Council count, resulting in two women being elected to the body. Ben Lohberger had been expected to take up the deputy lord mayor position but failed to win a councillor seat. Under the rules, the deputy lord mayor will instead be chosen by councillors at their first meeting.
items.title: Hobart council gains two women as deputy mayor-elect loses seat

items.summary: Nine people aboard a Learjet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas were killed when it crashed near Cresthaven and Greenacres in Palm Beach County on Sunday. The jet entered a steep dive after pilots reported turbulence and requested a climb. About 600 residents are being assisted with temporary shelter, according to the sheriff's office.
items.title: Learjet Crash Kills Nine in Florida Neighborhood

items.summary: A private Learjet 60 crashed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday, killing all nine aboard. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the aircraft departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas before nose-diving near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North and erupting into a fireball that just missed homes. The NTSB is investigating the cause.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Kills All Nine Aboard

items.summary: Indian authorities are preparing for Cyclone Murasu, expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Bapatla on November 3. Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to stay ready for relief operations as heavy to very heavy rain is forecast across parts of three states over the next days. Wind speeds up to 110 kmph are anticipated at landfall, with damage possible to around 15,128 electricity poles across 12 districts. Meanwhile, Odisha continues recovery from Cyclone Arnab, whose death toll rose to six on Sunday as two more bodies were recovered and search continued for 10 missing people.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu brace for Cyclone Murasu

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion, aged 20, after finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix. His championship lead reached an unbeatable 119 points. He is also the first Italian driver to win since 1953. The race was stopped by a red flag with 25 of the 71 laps remaining before being restarted; Max Verstappen won and Lewis Hamilton finished second.
items.title: Antonelli Becomes Youngest F1 World Champion at 20

items.summary: Anantapur superintendent of police Jagadeesh told PTI that Hemant, accused of attacking two Class 10 girls with a chainsaw at a government school in Raptadu on October 31, was hiding near the Atmakur forest. Police formed 15 teams and fired around six rounds after he assaulted officers; one inspector was injured. One girl lost her right hand.
items.title: Police Shoot and Nab Chainsaw Attacker in Atmakur Forest

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, saying if Gandhi wanted to become prime minister he should remain in a “mock parliament” his whole life. Shah said the Congress had lost elections for 15 years and that Sonia Gandhi’s dream of seeing her son as PM remained unfulfilled. He also accused the party of obstructing Parliament over women’s reservation and organising the rally on November 1, linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The rally came amid a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Amit Shah dismisses Rahul Gandhi as a permanent opposition figure

items.summary: Videos captured a business jet carrying nine people exploding into a fireball near a busy road in Greenacres, Palm Beach County, Florida. US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said all aboard died as cited by AP. Air traffic control recordings show the pilot reporting icing and turbulence before declaring an emergency descent of up to 30,000 feet per minute. The FAA is assisting the NTSB investigation.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Kills All Nine Aboard Near Busy Roadway

items.summary: St. Joseph's Church at Perumpannaiyur in Tiruvarur district, built from 1871 and standing about 153 feet tall, is estimated to need Rs 40 crore for a restoration project expected to run roughly three years after beginning in April 2026. The parish has appealed to the public, philanthropists, devotees and government for financial help. Financial strain is compounded by alleged encroachment of church land by a politician, reducing revenue from more than 250 acres it owns.
items.title: Century-old Tamil Nadu church seeks Rs 40 crore restoration after land encroachment

items.summary: EkChitra Art Gallery opened Living Temple II, its second edition celebrating Indian art heritage through over 100 works by more than 30 artists. Founder Annapurna Madipadiga framed the event as a dialogue between ancient knowledge and contemporary expression. Attendee Shilpa Reddy called both editions fortunate experiences, praising Nagendra Babu's 32-foot scroll and an M.S. Subbulakshmi saree collection. The exhibition runs until 29 November 2026.
items.title: Living Temple II Opens at EkChitra Art Gallery

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest world champion, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record and becoming the first Italian winner since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver secured the 2026 drivers' title with a third-place finish at Mexico City after four rounds remained. Max Verstappen won ahead of Hamilton, while Antonelli needed only ninth place or better to clinch it. He said he would not be there without Mercedes and his family.
items.title: Antonelli Claims F1 Title as Youngest Ever Champion

items.summary: A month ago, reports claimed oil flows out of Hormuz had recovered to pre-war levels and pushed prices lower, but the rout did not last. Brent benchmarks are set for a fourth monthly gain in a row as Gulf states say they export more than before the war. JP Morgan's Natasha Kaneva told the Wall Street Journal that her model suggests fair value at $94 per barrel of Brent crude, yet it trades above $116. Shipping costs have soared to all-time highs and producing countries discount their oil despite reports about improving flows. UBS strategist Giovanni Staunovo noted a sharp deterioration in maritime security as vessels face attacks and insurance and freight costs rise. The International Energy Agency's Fatih Birol said the disruption will likely continue well into next year, with no credible pathway back to pre-war prices.
items.title: Oil Prices Decouple From Headlines Amid War Premium

items.summary: At the 71st Foundation Day function in Bhopal, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said Madhya Pradesh was entering a new era of development. He highlighted an industrial growth rate that had reached around 24%, attributing progress to youth, women and farmers. The state ranked third nationally in milk production and received Rs 490 crore in MSME subsidies.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Cites Industrial Growth At Bhopal Foundation Day Event

items.summary: A car salesman in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh was jailed after being produced before a court on Sunday. Identified as Gajendra alias Rishi Anand, he was arrested by Ashoka Garden police on Saturday following the theft of a luxury car worth Rs 23 lakh from a showroom on September 28. Police say his wife's desire to drive expensive cars motivated him.
items.title: Bhopal Salesman Arrested for Stealing Luxury Car to Fulfil Wife's Wish

items.summary: Villa Vie Residences abruptly ended an indefinite ocean cruise after roughly two years, telling passengers they had less than seven hours notice and to leave by 2 o'clock. Passengers Randy Cassingham and his wife were stranded in Cambodia, the ship's 65th country visited. The company said fuel prices rose three to four times since a war began in Iran; Cassingham disputed that as the full cause, saying the company had been in financial trouble from the start. He paid $379,000 for a cabin with at least 15 years of sailing guaranteed.
items.title: Cruise Ship Ends After Two Years Over Fuel Costs

items.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary appealed on Sunday to affluent households and income-tax-paying people in the state to voluntarily give up their benefit of 125 units of free electricity, he said. He addressed the two-day Pataliputra National Youth Parliament-2.0 in Patna, saying such contributions would help Bihar's development. Choudhary noted the subsidy costs around Rs 23,000 crore annually and runs at about Rs 8,000-10,000 per household.
items.title: Bihar Chief Minister Urges Wealthy Households and Taxpayers to Surrender Free Power Benefit

items.summary: The Election Commission ordered immediate suspension of Electoral Registration Officers Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary over alleged irregularities in the 127-Pilibhit Assembly constituency electoral roll. An inquiry found a computer assistant submitted 13,779 Form 8 applications between May 31 and August 29; 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. No application forms or supporting documents were located in the office. The Commission directed chargesheets for scrutiny barring reinstatement without approval, added Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita to an existing FIR against them and operator Anil Kumar, ordered rigorous case pursuit, verification across constituencies, and termination of the outsourced computer assistant's services.
items.title: Election Commission Suspends Two Pilibhit Poll Officers Over Voter Roll Irregularities

items.summary: Police remained on duty in central Frankfurt on Sunday, 1 November, after riots broke out following a demonstration the previous day. Footage shows smashed shop windows, looted stores and burning barricades across the streets. Several protesters and officers were injured while 30 people were detained. The situation calmed by early morning after police cordoned off parts of the city centre. Violence was also reported in Cologne and Berlin.
items.title: Riots Erupt in Frankfurt After Demonstration, Police Respond With Water Cannon

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar helped Narendra Modi secure a third term and Amit Shah become home minister, calling the alleged voter-roll deletion “treason” and demanding Kumar’s removal. The rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan drew INDIA bloc leaders and several chief ministers; Mamata Banerjee said her party was made to lose in Bengal, while BJP leader JP Nadda called it a conspiracy to instigate riots. Gandhi accused the BJP of shutting shops near Connaught Place.
items.title: INDIA bloc leaders rally demanding removal of election commissioner over alleged vote theft

items.summary: Hundreds of young demonstrators gathered outside Berlin's Brandenburg Gate on Saturday as part of a nationwide day of youth protests organised by the GenZ regelt! movement. The rally was one of demonstrations planned in more than 30 German cities, including Frankfurt and Cologne, following student protests across several European countries.
items.title: Youth Protesters Gather at Berlin's Brandenburg Gate

items.summary: Protests in France have helped inspire youth demonstrations across Europe, from Portugal and Italy to Germany, according to a report by Charlotte Hughes. In Germany, large Saturday rallies led by an initiative loosely translating as “Gen Z has got this” called for better education and healthcare, stronger climate protection, lower living costs, and opposed reinstating compulsory military service. Demonstrations in several major German cities turned violent late in the day, particularly in Frankfurt.
items.title: Youth-led rallies sweep Europe amid German unrest

items.summary: One week before South Africa's local elections, residents across Johannesburg describe crumbling pavements and roads choked with rubbish, foul-smelling water at the Jukskei River, widespread power cuts and potholes. Semadi Manganye of Alexandra Water Warriors says challenges range from electricity to waste, while Kate Spiller calls the water situation
items.title: Anger mounts over Johannesburg's failing infrastructure ahead of local elections

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, promoter of the Mahadev Online Book app and alleged kingpin of an illegal betting syndicate, from Oman. A special CBI team brought him to India after he was located by the Royal Oman Police following an Interpol Red Corner Notice. He will be produced in Raipur on Monday, undergo a medical examination, and face chargesheets filed under several laws; the CBI described the extradition as significant for bringing transnational fugitives to justice.
items.title: CBI Extradites Mahadev Betting App Promoter From Oman

items.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan was sent to 14-day jail custody after bail in the dual PAN card case, arrested by the Enforcement Directorate over a money laundering probe linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The ED told the court he is withholding evidence needed to trace alleged proceeds of crime. On October 28, authorities provisionally attached university land and buildings valued at Rs 426. 46 crore originally and around Rs 1,170 crore now; an assessment put construction cost at Rs 494. 46 crore across 59 buildings, raising total campus valuation to Rs 499. 09 crore against only Rs 78.
items.title: Azam Khan Sent to Custody in Jauhar University Money Laundering Case

items.summary: EL PAÍS USA Edition reports on an InsideHook essay by New York writer Jaed Coffin, who frames declining male hormone levels not as crisis but as grounds for self-acceptance. The piece notes that the average man’s testosterone fell 54% between 1972 and 2019, per a study presented in London at an ESHRE meeting covering around 118,000 men from five countries. It then surveys how public figures — Robert F. Kennedy Jr., J.D. Vance, Scott Galloway, Andrew Tate — have linked masculinity to hormones or politics, and reports the University of Sydney’s analysis that social media is pushing hormone therapy on healthy young men. The article offers no single conclusion beyond describing these competing narratives.
items.title: A Spanish outlet reframes low testosterone as a celebrated identity

items.summary: Since Abdel Fattah al-Sisi took power, Egypt has invested heavily in monumental projects meant to rival ancient achievements and restore the country among leading nations. Cairo now hosts the Grand Egyptian Museum, billed as its largest museum for a single civilization; infrastructure including the 220-foot Tahya Misr bridge certified by Guinness World Records; and the New Administrative Capital with an African-tallest skyscraper and a world-record flagpole since 2021. In July, a new military headquarters called the Octagon was inaugurated, covering 35 square miles and surpassing the Pentagon in size and name. Officials describe these works as embracing tradition while building toward national prominence.
items.title: Egypt pursues pharaonic megaprojects under Sisi's New Republic vision

items.summary: The French Business Cycle Dating Committee (CDCEF) of the French Economic Association (AFSE), led by Laurent Ferrara, released a statement on 10/29/2026 assessing recent French GDP data. The quarterly growth rate for the third quarter of 2026 stands at −0.1%, following a contraction of 0.2% in the first quarter and stagnation in the second. Some commentators argue this sequence implies a technical recession over the first three quarters of 2026, but the CDCEF urges caution, noting GDP figures remain subject to revision and that recessions require evaluating duration, depth and diffusion rather than two negative quarters alone. Cumulative decline since late 2025 is around 0.3%, far below past crises. The committee concludes current data do not support a recession, though sluggish activity warrants monitoring.
items.title: French economic association rules out recession amid near-zero growth

items.summary: CleanTechnica's Zach and Scott modeled two hypothetical Norwegian coastal bulk services to test whether GMI Group's hydrogen-electric ships make economic sense. Over fifteen years, they found hydrogen propulsion 50–58% more expensive than diesel even with roughly €13.1 million in public support assumed upfront, while battery-electric options were cheaper by about €11.64–14.13 million. The results are scenario-based, not GMI's actual contracts; the company has not published route or commercial data needed for a direct assessment.
items.title: Modeler Finds Hydrogen Bulk Carriers Costlier Than Batteries on Two Routes

items.summary: Paul Krugman and Heather Cox Richardson recently posted on Substack, drawing on earlier warnings from GOP media consultant Rick Wilson to argue that Donald Trump may act destructively after losing the midterms. Krugman cites Robert Pape’s ‘gambling for resurrection’ idea, suggesting a politically bankrupt Trump has incentives to provoke upheaval. Richardson points to reports of proposed Putin–Xi talks over Ukraine and quotes Tom Nichols on Trump abandoning Western order, while also noting Andrew McCarthy’s claim that Trump gives aid and comfort to Russia. Both writers frame the situation as an existential threat rooted in what they call political bankruptcy.
items.title: Krugman and Richardson Revive Rick Wilson’s Trump Warning

items.summary: Boehm, Levchenko and Xiang model optimal tariffs with a time-to-build lag in firm creation. Protection raises future domestic firms but costs higher prices now. Without commitment to future tariffs, short-run price concerns preserve freer trade and derail manufacturing growth.
items.title: Time-Inconsistent Tariffs Undermine Manufacturing Renaissance in Model

items.summary: The Trump administration set a November 29 deadline for concluding a trade probe launched in May over alleged intellectual property violations, designating Vietnam as the first priority foreign country in 13 years. Industry groups accuse Vietnam of unfair practices, piracy and inadequate enforcement. Meanwhile, Vietnam's exports to the US surged 42% through eight months this year versus 2025, making it the largest goods-surplus partner ahead of China and Mexico.
items.title: Tesla and Samsung Back US Tariff Probe Against Vietnam

items.summary: The First Dog on the Moon cartoon poses a question about Google's AI summary, suggesting it may damage the company's profits. The piece asks whether this development helps or hurts Google and implies that its own search has become less handy.
items.title: First Dog on the Moon questions whether Google search is still useful

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday he had a good conversation with US President Donald Trump about the future of Canada-US trade, building on recent constructive discussions toward a mutually beneficial deal. Trump added his administration has the concept of an agreement benefiting farmers. The two leaders have exchanged messages as tariffs and talks continue amid uncertainty over timelines.
items.title: Carney and Trump Signal Progress on Canada-US Trade Deal

items.summary: John Ternus will host his first Apple earnings call on Monday, with investors weighing whether a wave of new products can offset surging memory-chip costs. The company has shipped its first foldable phone, smart home hub and touch-screen laptops this fiscal quarter. Analysts expect profit growth to fall to its weakest in six quarters as holiday-quarter results approach.
items.title: Apple's new CEO Ternus faces first earnings test amid rising memory costs

items.summary: US technology shares had their worst selloff in months last week as disappointing quarterly results raised doubts about whether heavy AI spending will pay off. Alphabet led the rout, with its stock falling 13% on October 29 after revenue of $127.6 billion missed expectations and earnings came in at $2.12 versus a forecast of $3.02. The pain spread to chipmakers, including Intel's 29% plunge on October 30, as analysts cited growing concerns over AI profitability.
items.title: Alphabet's Weak Earnings Trigger Tech Sell-Off

items.summary: Connecticut launched LEAP in summer 2021, sending school personnel on home visits to chronically absent students across its 15 most disadvantaged districts. Brunner, Jiang and Ross estimate attendance rose about 4–5 percentage points while chronic absenteeism fell 13–15 points; effects held steady after correcting for selection.
items.title: Connecticut Home Visits Boost Attendance for Absent Students

items.summary: Reports indicate Apple is preparing updates for three iPad models, including the entry-level tablet, iPad Air and iPad Pro, with launches expected in the first half of 2027. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says Apple is now focusing on its remaining tablets after updating the iPad mini with an OLED display in October. The company has not confirmed these changes.
items.title: Apple reportedly plans iPad lineup refresh in first half of 2027

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on the Cheeky Pint podcast that keeping DRAM in personal computers is 'quite terrible,' arguing memory ends up being used 5% of the time versus high cloud utilisation. Elon Musk replied, 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!' The piece then shifts to a broader memory shortage pushing up prices across phones, laptops and consoles.
items.title: Altman Calls Personal RAM a Waste; Musk Fires Back Over Memory Shortage

items.summary: Actor Ranbir Kapoor drew a playful comparison between Elon Musk's newly showcased flying Tesla Roadster and the Pushpaka Vimana from the Ramayana, saying India had invented a flying vehicle 5,000 years ago. He made the remark during a promotional interaction for Ramayana, scheduled to release on November 5.
items.title: Ranbir Kapoor Compares India's Ancient Flying Vehicle to Musk's Tesla Roadster

items.summary: Share markets steadied across Asia on Monday as investors awaited Apple earnings, hoping for relief from AI cash-burn worries while oil prices eased after talks continued between Iranian and Qatari mediators. Apple shares have climbed four months straight to unseat Nvidia as the world's most valuable listed company. Analysts expect quarterly EPS of $2 on revenue of $113 billion, up from $1.85 a year earlier. Optimism helped S&P 500 futures edge up 0.4 per cent and Nasdaq futures bounce 0.8 per cent after October's worst month since April 2025. Goldman Sachs analysts expect hyperscaler capex to almost double to $800 billion this year, rising to $1.2 trillion in 2027. Ben Snider wrote that earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating.
items.title: Asian Shares Steady on Apple Earnings Hopes and Falling Oil

items.summary: Shares of supermarket operator Sheng Siong fell over 9% to a one-year low after the group reported a marginal 1.9 per cent rise in third-quarter net profit, reaching S$44.6 million from S$43.7 million. Revenue rose 6.2 per cent to S$441.5 million. Management cited competition ahead of the RTS Link and rising labour costs as challenges. DBS analyst Chee Zheng Feng expects further earnings moderation in the fourth quarter.
items.title: Sheng Siong Shares Hit One-Year Low on Weak Outlook

items.summary: Elon Musk acknowledged that xAI reduced compute for its autonomous agent, Grok Bot, because serving it costs more than subscription revenue recoups. Speaking on X after a subscriber requested an early quota reset, he said the cost of running the tool was unsustainably high relative to revenue and offered no scaling promise or timetable. The admission breaks with rivals who quietly throttle capacity while competitors like OpenAI do likewise; analysts note AI token margins must exceed 100% between 2026 and 2030, and reports cite a growing share of abandoned AI projects.
items.title: Elon Musk Admits Grok Bot Is Unprofitable

items.summary: Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's head of data center energy, told The Information that building data centers in orbit could be as much as 100 times costlier than on the ground. She urged exhausting terrestrial options first and framed space as a long-term experiment rather than an immediate fix for Earth-based power constraints.
items.title: Google Energy Chief Warns Space Data Centers Could Cost Far More

items.summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) launched a WhatsApp service for PF members, but users reported it was not working properly within hours of the rollout. Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya introduced the service at EPFO's 74th Foundation Day event in New Delhi on Saturday. The service lets subscribers check their balance and passbook details.
items.title: EPFO WhatsApp Service Draws Complaints on Launch Day

items.summary: Gold rose as much as 0.7% toward nearly US$3,900 an ounce after a 3.7% drop the prior session and its worst October since 2008. Spot gold climbed 0.6% to US$3,899.39 in Singapore at 7.45am. Strategist Justin Lin of Global X ETFs cited dip buying but warned of precarious levels; Ole Sloth Hansen of Saxo Bank AS noted technical selling and vulnerability below US$3,886, with a recovery above US$4,000 needed for neutrality.
items.title: Gold Rebounds From One-Year Low on Dip Buying

items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung announced during his annual budget speech that South Korea will spend 21.3 trillion won ($16 billion) on chipmaking and artificial intelligence in 2027, nearly double this year's amount, to build a smart military force.
items.title: South Korea Doubles AI and Chip Spending in 2027

items.summary: EAAA India Alternatives Ltd shares are set to list on the BSE and NSE at a grey market premium of Rs 54 per share, or about 3%, over the upper price band of Rs 1,665. The Rs 1,200 crore IPO was an offer for sale with no fresh equity issuance, so all proceeds go to selling shareholder Edelweiss Securities & Investments Pvt. Overall subscription stood at 5. 51 times, led by QIBs at 13. 80 times. Based on FY26 diluted EPS, the issue carried a P/E of about 40 times versus an industry peer average of 39. 89 times. The company reported total income of Rs 964 crore and PAT of Rs 265 crore in FY26. Axis Capital Ltd. , Jefferies India Pvt. Ltd. , Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Ltd. and Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd. acted as book-running lead managers, with MUFG Intime India Pvt. Ltd. as registrar.
items.title: EAAA India Alternatives Shares List at Under-1% Premium

items.summary: The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity concluded in Yerevan, Armenia, after negotiators agreed its main decisions, including the Yerevan Pathway aimed at accelerating global biodiversity action. Held halfway between the adoption and 2030 deadline of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, whose review warned that targets would not be met without faster implementation, the pathway focuses on strengthening efforts to meet existing commitments rather than setting new ones. Nearly $2 billion in new funding was announced by the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity, alongside a report finding developed countries had failed to provide at least $20 billion annually as promised for 2025. Officials said the next four years will determine whether governments can turn commitments into measurable progress before the deadline. As Schomaker put it: "Ultimately, the test is not what governments agreed in Yerevan, but what they change when they return home."
items.title: COP17 Concludes With Yerevan Pathway for Biodiversity Action

items.summary: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) members, including two from Punjab—Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra—took part in a gathering where they chanted 'BJP Zindabad' at the Bharatiya Janata Party's Delhi headquarters. Suspended AAP MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resigned from the Punjab Assembly, having left the Arvind Kejriwal-led party days earlier and joined BJP on Monday. The move drew criticism from ruling Punjab AAP president Aman Arora, who accused BJP of inducting leaders expelled or departed from other parties (attribution: named).
items.title: Big setback ahead of Punjab polls: AAP MLAs chant 'BJP Zindabad' at Delhi HQ, set to join party

items.summary: Around 2.5 lakh shops across roughly 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi stayed closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore after the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan disrupted business during peak Diwali shopping. CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of about three lakh shops remained shut amid traffic restrictions and crowd concerns, while roughly 5,000 vehicles could not carry goods to Old Delhi and Central Delhi markets. He noted the affected markets generate around Rs 10,000-12,000 crore during this season. The Automotive Parts Merchant Association opposed the venue's timing, and Rahul Gandhi urged rally participants to shop from local traders while accusing the BJP of spreading rumours about economic harm.
items.title: Delhi Traders Blame INDIA Bloc Rally for Diwali Business Losses

items.summary: Robert Hux, Canadian Director of Schiller Institute, praised China's governance achievements, highlighting poverty eradication and rural infrastructure development. He made the comments following the conclusion of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, which set out plans to further strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance.
items.title: Schiller Institute's Robert Hux Praises China Governance Gains

items.summary: Professional bodies representing counsellors and psychotherapists are calling for statutory regulation in the UK to protect the public from abuse, according to a report hailed as a watershed moment. Unlike doctors or midwives, these titles are not protected nor regulated, allowing anyone to practise without qualification even after misconduct. The Commission for the Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy launched an independent review in October 2025. It estimates about 1.8 million people on waiting lists could fill a treatment gap, with practitioners able to provide more than 370,000 hours of therapy weekly. Campaigner Ella Janneh cited her own case as evidence. Co-chairs Phil Hope and Andrea Sutcliffe argue the government should act given the compelling harm testimony.
items.title: Counsellors and Psychotherapists Urge UK Statutory Regulation

items.summary: A Commons business, innovation, science and trade select committee report concludes the UK is shaping its policy on China “as it goes along” since 2024, risking a strategy dictated by Washington or Beijing. Liam Byrne, Labour MP and chair of the committee, said the piecemeal approach endangers British firms’ EU business and misses opportunities while leaving risks unmanaged. The report cites March’s decision to block Ming Yang from building a £1.5bn wind plant in Scotland as an example of reactivity. It calls for clear new rules, including red and green zones for Chinese investment, amid pressure on the UK to align with EU tariffs on electric vehicles.
items.title: UK MPs Warn Over Ad Hoc China Policy

items.summary: Mitsui Fudosan is pursuing a mixed-use real estate project on land near the British Library, seeking profit from strong London demand while strengthening its brand presence. Kanako Komura, development director at Mitsui Fudosan UK, said the company can leverage expertise in domestic and overseas urban development and large-scale mixed-use projects. The firm cites past redevelopments, including a 52-floor Tokyo Midtown building and a $5 billion Tsukiji site project.
items.title: Mitsui Fudosan Bets on British Library Mixed-Use Project in London

items.summary: Outdoor music events at Tanjong Pagar Distripark have paused after noise complaints from neighbours, organisers said. The Keppel Road venue hosts Ice Cream Sundays by the independent collective Cream Team since 2023; co-founder Jake Camacho was told on Oct 16 that outdoor music could not continue under tighter restrictions. Owner Mapletree posted an Instagram message acknowledging loud music may cause disamenity and asked licensees to pause events, without specifying a duration or names. The group said it had already moved its final Oct 3 event back in the carpark and reduced noise measures. Organisers noted venues are scarce at affordable rates as other sites like Haw Par Villa close after redevelopment; Culture SG's Vira Suria echoed that losing such spaces makes things harder for independent organisers.
items.title: Noise complaints force pause of outdoor music events at Tanjong Pagar Distripark

items.summary: The author, who describes themselves as not religious, examines why people feel grief and mourn the death of those believed to be heading to heaven. They note that mourning is sincere but question whether celebrating a departure toward heaven should instead bring happiness. The author suggests this tension reflects mood management: people construct portfolios mixing positive and negative emotions during stressful situations, adjusting their emotional balance as needed rather than staying consistent over time. This same pattern, the author argues, appears in debates about AI, where people hold both love and dislike for models to avoid a non-diversified emotional portfolio.
items.title: Author Questions Grief for Those Heading to Heaven

items.summary: Niklas Persson, CEO of grid integration at Hitachi Energy, tells Euronews Earth that consumers can become “better grid citizens” by using electricity more intelligently rather than simply consuming less. He notes the technology already exists and calls for a partnership between governments, utilities, businesses and consumers to upgrade transmission networks and accelerate permitting. The piece situates this within rising European gas prices expected to stay high into next year, an AI-driven surge in data centres, and smart-meter uptake of 5.9 per cent in Germany — up just 1.5 per cent over six months. Ember cites that smart EV charging could absorb around three per cent of peak wind and solar generation in Spain, where about 10 per cent of monthly power was curtailed in May 2026.
items.title: Hitachi Energy CEO Frames Europeans as Active Grid Participants Amid Rising Prices

items.summary: With the first Harry Potter film marking its 25th anniversary in November, Rail Europe has selected five real-life locations across the UK where fans can experience filming backdrops. The list includes Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross station in London; Warner Bros. Studio Tour London in Hertfordshire, home to “Hogwarts in the Snow,” running from 14 November 2026 to 17 January 2027; Glenfinnan Viaduct in Scotland; Oxford filming sites such as the Bodleian Library’s Divinity School and Christ Church staircase; Durham cathedral; and Goathland station on North Yorkshire Moors Railway. Trains from London take around 45 minutes to Oxford and about three hours to Durham, with heritage trains running seasonally at some sites.
items.title: Five UK Train Journeys Inspired by Harry Potter

items.summary: Scroll is launching a report investigating whether Mumbai and Kolkata developers and authorities disclose the risk of sea-level-driven home loss to buyers. Citing the United Nations, it says up to 14 million people could lose homes to rising seas. The team plans to map vulnerable areas and check if coastal development destroyed natural buffers like mangroves.
items.title: Mumbai and Kolkata coastal flooding risk investigation by Scroll

items.summary: An article compares how Western outlets covered two October student movements, one in India led by the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, and another against education funding cuts in France. It argues coverage diverged: Indian reporting emphasised police action, with headlines citing over 2,000 protesters detained on 10 October, while French coverage centred demonstrators' accounts amid allegations of excessive force. Media experts Pradip K Bagchi and Abhijit Mazumdar suggest Western media bias toward the Global South shapes such framing. The piece notes figures like 400,000 protesters across France were reported without attributing them to a single source.
items.title: Western Media Framed India and France Student Protests Differently

items.summary: The Madras High Court ruled that non-Hindus who refuse to pledge reverence or follow traditional customs cannot enter Agamic temples in Tamil Nadu, saying such entry would compromise the shrines' sanctity. In a public interest litigation filed by K Thangam Venkatesh, the bench comprising Justices G R Swaminathan and P Murugan directed strict enforcement of temple-entry rules without political concession. The court distinguished its inclusive approach from performative displays of faith for vote value, citing examples including Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's entry after signing an undertaking, while directing authorities to uphold age-old customs.
items.title: Madras HC Bars Non-Hindus With Religious Markers From Agamic Temples

items.summary: The Bishop of Wollongong announced that St Michael's Catholic primary school in Mittagong would amalgamate with St Thomas Aquinas in Bowral and close by 2029, becoming Corpus Christi Catholic Parish Primary School. More than 1,600 people have signed a petition opposing the move, which parents say left them blindsided after they were not consulted. The closure follows an assessment of enrolment trends, demographic data and long-term financial viability; no decision has yet been made on the Mittagong site's future use from 2029. Parents, teachers and union representatives have called for a review of the decision.
items.title: Parents oppose closure of historic Mittagong Catholic primary school

items.summary: A sports coach acquitted of making a child amenable to sexual activity has been barred from working with children. A tribunal heard he sent a teenager more than 140 Facebook messages showing an inappropriate and overly familiar pattern of communication, posing what it called an unacceptable risk of harm to children. The ban was upheld.
items.title: Sports coach banned from working with children after tribunal

items.summary: NTPC reported second-quarter FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 45,752 crore, up nearly 17% year-on-year. The company also announced a first interim dividend of Rs 3 per share with November 6 set as the record date. Shares rose more than 5% in a week. Jefferies maintained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 425 and raised FY27 EPS by 1%. Nuvama Institutional Equities kept its Buy call at Rs 400, citing strong power demand. The article carries disclaimers that the writer is not SEBI-registered and views are those of the brokerages.
items.title: NTPC shares climb on Q2 results as Jefferies and Nuvama stay bullish

items.summary: A five-month real-time facial recognition trial in Western Australia scanned 1,380,882 faces across 100 deployments, producing 122 arrests and nine incorrect alerts. WA police commissioner Col Blanch said no one was arrested over the false matches but that officers engaged each person. Civil Liberties Australia's Bill Rowlings criticised the error rate framing, arguing it should be measured against convictions while scans occurred without reasonable suspicion.
items.title: WA Facial Recognition Trial Yields 122 Arrests Amid Privacy Criticism

items.summary: Murasu is the name given by the India Meteorological Department to a cyclonic storm heading toward Andhra Pradesh. The word comes from Tamil and refers to a large traditional war drum used during celebrations, warfare and warning of danger. It follows Cyclone Arnab in the North Indian Ocean naming sequence, which contains 169 names contributed equally by each of 13 participating countries and assigned alphabetically rather than by destination. Names must be short, easy to pronounce and politically neutral. A storm receives its name once sustained winds reach at least 34 knots or about 62 kmph.
items.title: The Tamil drum behind cyclone Murasu's name

items.summary: The Delhi Jal Board plans a ₹149 crore, 8.34-km sewer rising main through the ecologically sensitive Yamuna floodplain to curb recurring sewage overflows from three ageing gravity ducts built in 1938, 1972 and 1992. The pipeline has received administrative approval of its estimated cost of ₹148.90 crore, with bids invited on October 26 for a project valued at approximately ₹140.04 crore over 1.5 years. Yamuna activist Bhim Singh Rawat warns that construction in encroached floodplains harms the river ecosystem long-term.
items.title: DJB Approves Yamuna Floodplain Sewer Line Amid Environmental Concerns

items.summary: Nearly 7,000 people attended a free marriage registration camp at the Harahara Mahadeva Temple in Karanthur, near Kozhikode, on November 1, far exceeding organisers' expectations. The queue stretched across two bus stops along the National Highway, prompting police to manage crowds and traffic. Organisers had arranged only 1,500 forms but printed thousands more as demand surged within hours. Press Trust of India reported that about 80 per cent of registrants were men, with many women seeking second marriages; participants said it offered hope after years of unsuccessful searches.
items.title: Kerala Temple Marriage Camp Draws Record Crowd of 7,000

items.summary: On Sunday, November 2, 2026, US President Donald Trump held rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans made a final push ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. In Salina, Kansas, he urged voters to elect Republican House and Senate candidates on November 3rd, promising continued America-first policies if they retain control of Congress. He also endorsed Sen. Roger Marshall and Ty Masterson.
items.title: Trump Holds Final Weekend Rallies Before Midterms

items.summary: Heavy rainfall from Cyclone Murasu affected northern Tamil Nadu as the severe cyclonic storm approached the coast of Tamil Nadu and South Andhra Pradesh. Chennai Airport cancelled at least 11 flights on Monday due to adverse weather conditions, including routes between Chennai-Vijayawada, Rajahmundry, Kadapa and Tiruchirappalli. Greater Chennai Corporation commissioner Sameeran reported no major incidents despite widespread rainfall.
items.title: Cyclone Murasu Cancellations and Rainfall in Tamil Nadu

items.summary: Nearly 3,000 migrants have reached El Hierro in Spain’s Canary Islands since early October, according to unattributed reporting. On October 22, more than 400 people arrived on four boats from the African coast, per maritime rescue services. Residents fear pressure on infrastructure and resources, with some citing water costs and perceptions of free assistance for migrants. The situation has entered Spain’s political debate ahead of general elections scheduled for November 29.
items.title: El Hierro residents weigh options amid rising migrant arrivals

items.summary: In Andhra Pradesh, police shot a 21-year-old man on Sunday as he allegedly tried to escape custody after attacking a Class 10 schoolgirl with a chainsaw. Several officers were injured; the girl was moved 200 km to Bengaluru for treatment. Separately, Uttar Pradesh Police fired at another suspect in Mathura who opened fire during an anti-murder search operation.
items.title: Police Shoot Two Suspects While Allegedly Fleeing Custody in India

items.summary: A statement by Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh on October 2 gave a fresh twist to the alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah, bringing Union minister HD Kumaraswamy’s Delhi residence into the investigation. Accused Ritesh Pandey reportedly confessed that a mobile phone used in the operation was bought in Karol Bagh and handed over to Prajwal Prasad at Kumaraswamy’s official residence. The video surfaced on September 27, alleging sexual abuse linked to an incident in 2011. While the disclosure has put Kumaraswamy in a politically uncomfortable position amid his own allegations against Shivakumar, police caution that responsibility cannot yet be fixed and warn against drawing conclusions before digital evidence is verified (s34). The final answer remains awaited as investigators examine financial transactions and CCTV footage (s42-43).
items.title: Probe trail reaches Kumaraswamy’s Delhi home in Siddaramaiah sting case

items.summary: French prosecutors have launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during unrest, French media reported. An image of a Paris officer with his leg on fire prompted outrage and follows weeks of protests over the cost of living. The burned gendarme told Le Figaro the device had far greater burning capacity than a standard Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called throwing such a cocktail at police "a murder attempt." On Saturday there were more than 770 arrests, roughly half the previous week's total.
items.title: France Opens Attempted Murder Probe After Petrol Bomb Set Officer Alight

items.summary: Protesters clashed with security forces in Kangpokpi district after mutilated bodies of two missing youths were found stuffed in gunny bags on a banana farm in Senapati. Police fired tear gas and baton-charged the agitators, injuring one protester whose condition is stable. Deputy Chief Ministers Nemcha Kipgen and Losii Dikho condemned the killings and demanded investigation. Over 50 people have been killed since February clashes between Kuki and Naga communities, while earlier Meitei-Kuki violence claimed over 300 lives. Tribal groups seek an impartial probe into the deaths.
items.title: Protests Erupt in Manipur After Two Missing Kuki Youths Found Dead

items.summary: India's total coal imports declined by 5.83 per cent in August 2026, falling to 104.57 million tonnes from 111.05 million tonnes a year earlier. Imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants dropped sharply by 35.23 per cent. Union Coal Minister G Kishan Reddy said the decline reflects efforts to boost domestic production and strengthen supply chains, reinforcing energy security.
items.title: India's coal imports fell 5.83% in August, minister says

items.summary: A temple committee's marriage-matching camp drew far more people than expected, with queues spilling across two bus stops along the National Highway and police called to manage traffic. Organisers had planned for 1,500 to 2,000 attendees but saw crowds arrive by 7 am, prompting early form distribution that ran into the evening. Nearly 80 per cent of registrants were men, many above 30, while some women sought second marriages. The committee said it would share an applicant list over about 10 to 20 days and hold future camps every Sunday from 7 am to 10 am starting after November 22.
items.title: Temple Marriage Camp Draws Thousands in Kerala

items.summary: The article argues that smart home technology should be chosen for return on investment rather than novelty, presenting five upgrades with genuine savings and three overengineered gadgets to skip. Smart thermostats like Nest and Ecobee use geofencing and motion sensors to ease HVAC automatically; households save around 10% on heating and 15% on cooling, plus utility rebates may apply. Water leak sensors can prevent damage from slow drips behind a washing machine or under a water heater, where the average residential claim costs more than $10,000.
items.title: Smart Home Devices That Save Money Versus Those Worth Skipping

items.summary: Semafor reports that The Daily Caller, co-founded by Tucker Carlson in 2010 as the Republican Party’s answer to The New York Times, has shifted sharply against Donald Trump’s war in Iran and toward criticism of Israel. Publisher Neil Patel told Semafor he faced aggressive donor pressure over the turn, though he declined to detail financial costs. Editor-in-Chief Amber Duke said the Iran war marked a turning point for conservatives. Critics accuse the outlet of antisemitism; Fox host Mark Levin called it “Al Jazeera in Arabic.” Former staff worry about its drift toward the ‘groyper’ wing and damage to its talent pipeline.
items.title: Daily Caller turns against Trump and Israel

items.summary: The author republished from Wonder Tools describes testing twelve AI agents to act proactively without prompts. Early favorites are Dots, Slashy, and Hark for calendar conflicts, email management, and design. Costs vary: some start free while ChatGPT's Pro plan is $100/month. The writer advises starting with one agent and checking ongoing costs before connecting accounts.
items.title: I auditioned 12 AI agents to be my chief of staff. Here’s how they compared

items.summary: A column profiles Katy Hoffman, a 33-year-old registered dietitian in Kansas City who gained attention by investigating billionaire Amy Griffin's memoir claims. Hoffman confronted Billy Bush at a wedding on Lanai and shared court documents and audio recordings online. Society figures reportedly listen to her posts without following them publicly. She describes herself as 'just a nosy lady' and credits the Griffin case with teaching her investigative journalism, though she feels intimidated by professional reporters now contacting her about her Patreon.
items.title: Kansas City dietitian becomes society sleuth behind Amy Griffin feud

items.summary: Four Indian brokerage analysts outline technical views as the Nifty index tests resistance at 23,200 after breaking above 22,800 and forming a higher bottom near 22,400. HDFC Securities suggests long positions on dips toward support, while TradeBulls notes improving momentum but flags caution since the index remains below its declining 50-day EMA near 23,170. Anand Rathi requires a decisive breakout above 23,200 plus broader market strength for a sustainable recovery, with immediate support at 22,600 and 22,400.
items.title: Analysts See Nifty's Next Move Hinging on Breakout Above 23,200

items.summary: Antonio Guterres said he was appalled by the death of Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami, an OHCHR employee arbitrarily detained by Houthis since June 6, 2024. He is the second UN worker to die in custody after a World Food Program staff member who died on Feb. 11, 2025.
items.title: UN chief condemns death of staff member in Houthi detention in Yemen

items.summary: BJP Union Minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of using an improperly made AI-generated image to depict a large crowd at the INDIA bloc's Sunday rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, which protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The allegation was posted on X without a specific image and has not yet received an official response from Congress.
items.title: Congress and BJP Clash Over AI Crowd Image at Ramlila Rally

items.summary: Delhi launched its winter pollution enforcement drive on November 1, inspecting nearly 15,000 vehicles and turning back 1,539 at city borders. Authorities issued 566 challans for PUCC violations worth Rs 56.6 lakh, plus Rs 2 lakh and Rs 9.8 lakh in other penalties, totaling Rs 68.4 lakh on the first day. Traffic police reported a marginal staff shortage amid an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan; Pankaj Rana said they sent back around six vehicles in five hours and suggested commuters use the metro. Residents like Unis Saifi took Ubers to avoid restrictions, while offices moved to 50% work-from-home until January 31, 2027.
items.title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Drive Fines Drivers, Turns Back Thousands of Vehicles

items.summary: Lindsay Clancy, accused of murdering her three children in 2023, will return to a Massachusetts court on Monday as defence and prosecution teams weigh whether the case should be retried. Her first trial ended in mistrial after a 12-person jury could not reach unanimity; she has not denied the killings but argues postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors insist they were intentional. Lawyers debate dismissal under Rule 25 or double jeopardy grounds versus pursuing justice for her children. Judge William Sullivan is expected to rule on motions and possibly set trial dates at a November hearing, with defence counsel Kevin Reddington noting he could not go to trial until June 2027 if retried.
items.title: Clancy's lawyers and prosecutors debate a retrial before Massachusetts judge

items.summary: Ahead of the US midterm elections, concern over government corruption has become a rare bipartisan consensus in an otherwise polarised electorate. A record 89% of Americans told Gallup that corruption is widespread, up from 73% in 2024 and higher than any other country except Lebanon, Peru, Ghana and Nigeria. In a Fox News Poll, worry about corruption (88%) edged out inflation (85%) and gas prices (83%). Distrust cuts across party lines: the Brennan Center for Justice found negative views toward Congress, Trump, Biden and the Supreme Court alike, with roughly two-thirds seeing it as embedded in institutions. Yet trust in local government remains high at 64%, unchanged since Gallup began polling over half a century ago. Candidates from both parties are leaning on anti-establishment messaging, though analysts say whether this translates into backlash is unclear (s40).
items.title: Americans See Corruption as Top Election Issue Amid Deep Distrust

items.summary: VinEnergo has commissioned a rooftop solar system integrated with battery storage in the Vung Ang Economic Zone, Ha Tinh, Vietnam. It will supply clean electricity to VinFast’s vehicle plant, the VinES and VG battery facilities under its first Direct Power Purchase Agreement installation. Company estimates put first-year generation at about 39 million kWh, cutting emissions by more than 25,000 tonnes annually.
items.title: VinEnergo Commits Rooftop Solar And Storage To Vietnamese Factories

items.summary: HYXI presented solar and energy storage solutions across residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale segments at Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026 in Greater Noida from October 22 to 24. At Hall 15, Booth C279, the company displayed microinverters, string inverters and energy storage systems alongside its HYXI Cloud monitoring platform. Ashish Bisht, Country Manager of HYXI, said India offers significant opportunities for smart solar solutions as the company seeks to expand its presence in the Indian market.
items.title: HYXI Showcases Solar and Storage Solutions at REI Expo 2026

items.summary: Inside Climate News examines whether Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro will be judged harshly for his data center record as he considers a 2028 presidential run. Over about 20 months, Shapiro moved from fast-tracking hyper-scale data centers to an executive order slowing development. Republican opponent Stacy Garrity used the shift in attacks without electoral gain, while polls suggest it remains a lasting vulnerability: this July’s Quinnipiac poll showed Shapiro at 56 percent approval overall but underwater on AI data centers (24 percent approve, 34 percent disapprove). Emerson and Muhlenberg College polls later found growing public concern. Shapiro introduced GRID standards in February, which critics called not legally binding; he then removed data centers from the Fast Track program in August using words like “greedy” and “predatory.” His office declined to directly answer questions about his motives. Observers remain divided on whether his pivot is genuine or political.
items.title: Shapiro’s Data Center Flip Faces Political Test

items.summary: Anthropic PBC aims to raise up to US$3.5 billion from Japanese investors in its initial public offering in the United States, per a Nov 2 regulatory filing. Mizuho Securities will manage the Japanese portion, with Goldman Sachs Group and other firms handling orders. The sale targets a market at a 14-year low for first-time offerings, as Anthropic tests appetite amid larger Meta and Alphabet plans.
items.title: Anthropic Plans Largest US IPO, Taps Japan for Up to $3.5 Billion

items.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal Mandaviya announced that EPF subscribers can access their balance, last five transactions and passbook through the EPFO's verified WhatsApp service. He also said accounts with balances up to Rs 1,000 will be settled automatically without individual claims. The average settlement time fell to 2.57 days in October 2026.
items.title: EPFO Launches WhatsApp Service and Inoperative-Account Settlement

items.summary: Infosys shares fell 2.6% to ₹1,154.20 on the National Stock Exchange on November 2, 2026. The company announced expansion of its Pocharam Development Center in Hyderabad with a new block adding 10,000 seats and targeting over 13,000 employees under a hybrid model. Shares slid amid broader weakness, down 29.17% year-to-date versus the Nifty 50's 11.16% fall.
items.title: Infosys Shares Slide as Hyderabad Campus Expansion Announced

items.summary:
On Monday, Abu Dhabi's ADNOC and AI firm G42 signed a deal with OpenAI to deploy advanced AI across the state energy firm's operations. ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber said it makes ADNOC the first energy-sector company to use OpenAI’s frontier technology. Altman called 'energy' among OpenAI's challenges, noting physical power would dominate costs. The announcement coincided with talks over OpenAI's $1.4 trillion valuation and UAE data centre plans amid regional tensions.

visual null
items.title: ADNOC and G42 Sign OpenAI Deal as Altman Visits UAE

items.summary: A filing reported on Monday that AI lab Anthropic will sell up to 552.9 billion yen ($3.5 billion) worth of shares to Japanese investors as part of its US public listing, TOKYO, Nov 2. The new shares would raise working capital and fund operating expenses and capital expenditure. The filing did not state the size or valuation of the IPO.
items.title: Anthropic Files Plan to Sell $3.5 Billion of Shares in Japan IPO

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said at the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference that advanced AI models are now mostly smarter than its smartest scientists and can perform much of white-collar work. He added that human judgment, creativity and accountability must stay central to deployment, warning against handing decisions over to AI.
items.title: Altman Says AI Models Now Mostly Outsmart Top Scientists

items.summary: Temple, a wearable startup founded by Zomato's Deepinder Goyal, claims its temple-worn device measures heart rate more accurately than the Apple Watch Series 12, Fitbit Air, Whoop MG, Garmin Forerunner 970 and Oura Ring 5. The company made these claims in an October 31 white paper it funded, ran and analysed itself; the study was not peer-reviewed, took place at a single Gurugram site with treadmill running only, and did not test cycling or everyday activity.
items.title: Temple Startup Claims Its Wearable Beats Apple Watch on Heart-Rate Accuracy

items.summary: Sergey Brin reportedly saw $29 billion wiped from his fortune in a day after Alphabet shares fell more than 12% to about $283.29 from $321.89, per Billionaires Africa. The drop followed weak search growth and heavy AI spending. Larry Page's unrealised loss pushed the founders' combined decline to nearly $60 billion.
items.title: Brin's Fortune Falls as Alphabet Shares Slide

items.summary: Journalist Michael Lewis, author of Moneyball and The Big Short, speaks with Guardian journalist Nosheen Iqbal about his new book Blockers. It follows the civil servants who resisted Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency as it attempted to dismantle the US government.
items.title: Michael Lewis Discusses His New Book Blockers With Nosheen Iqbal

items.summary: Indian I.T. stocks have regained attention amid profit-booking in global AI and semiconductor stocks, but the direction is unclear. Market expert Neeraj Dewan suggests the recent strength may reflect profit-taking rather than a lasting shift. The outlook for companies such as Infosys and TCS depends on whether they can turn AI opportunities into revenue growth.
items.title: I.T. Stocks Rally After AI Selloff; Outlook Uncertain for Infosys and TCS

items.summary: Private surveys showed Asian manufacturing expanded in October but slowed, with chip exporters China, Japan and South Korea easing. A Dai-ichi Life economist said strong chip demand masked soft spots that the prolonged Middle East conflict may now expose through higher fuel and food prices. The IMF projects Asia's growth moderating to 4.8% in 2026 and 4.4% in 2027, citing war-driven energy shocks.
items.title: Asian factory growth slows as AI optimism meets Middle East war strain

items.summary: John Ternus, Apple's new chief executive since September, will host his first earnings call on Monday as investors weigh whether a wave of new products can offset rising memory-chip costs. Analysts expect the July-September quarter to show its weakest profit growth in six quarters.
items.title: Apple's New CEO John Ternus Faces First Earnings Test Amid Memory Cost Surge

items.summary: Avdjiev, Forbes, Nenova and Santos analyse drivers of global imbalances across 28 economies in NBER Working Paper 35962 (2026). They find financial factors are the primary drivers at both horizons, with trade significant especially long-term. Valuation gains since 2010 boosted growth but raised vulnerability.
items.title: Unraveling the Cobweb of Global Imbalances: Drivers, Vulnerabilities and Adjustment Scenarios -- by Stefan Avdjiev, Kristin Forbes, Tsvetelina Nenova, Marjorie Santos

items.summary: Fairlie, Khanna, Loyalka and Sachdeva study faculty productivity under India's reservation policy reserving roughly 50% of hires. Reservation-category faculty have lower education, ranks and experience yet show no meaningful instructional-quality differences; students taught by them perform slightly better on course grades.
items.title: Affirmative Action, Faculty Productivity and Caste Interactions

items.summary: NVIDIA has released Auto Ontology, an open-source semantic layer under the Apache 2.0 license that builds a context layer from enterprise metadata so agents can write SQL against certified business definitions through MCP, CLI and API. The five-part system discovers ontologies, grounds metrics with trusted meaning, validates queries against lineage, exposes them via read-only tools (9 of them) capping results at 100 rows, and learns corrections back into the ontology. NVIDIA reports a 90% reduction in ontology creation time from its own testing, but no text-to-SQL accuracy scores are published; an eval harness ships instead of benchmarked results, so users must run benchmarks themselves to trust it.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Open Auto Ontology for AI Agent SQL

items.summary: The four-person crew of NASA's CHAPEA analog mission emerged after 378 days in isolation at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas. The simulated Mars expedition ran from October 19 until August 22, 2025, with participants living in a 158-square-meter habitat and performing tasks such as growing crops in simulated Martian soil while managing communication delays. Medical officer Ellen Ellis described it as “a hell of a year,” framing the exercise to inform future crewed missions.
