items.title: NASA Mars Analog Crew Completes 378-Day Isolation

items.summary: At the 10th German-Chinese Automotive Congress in Wolfsburg on October 30, 2026, about 600 representatives from China and Germany gathered to explore closer collaboration amid industry transformation. Officials described electrification, digitalization, artificial intelligence and autonomous driving as key drivers of change. Olaf Lies called the congress a strong signal for deeper cooperation; Thomas Schmall stressed maintaining dialogue between German and Chinese firms; Liu Minqiang said competition can help upgrade the sector. Hunan Province pitched its '5C' advantages to attract German investment, with Sany Group among companies present. The event coincided with the International Suppliers Fair.
items.title: Chinese and German auto firms deepen cooperation at Wolfsburg congress

items.summary: Chen Yuwen, a researcher at the International Cooperation Center of the National Development and Reform Commission, outlines how Chinese private enterprises support high-quality economic development. A November 1, 2018 symposium set six policy measures to ease tax burdens, financing difficulties and costs while protecting entrepreneurs' safety and property. The article notes that by end of April 2026, private firms in the 'four new' sectors reached 24.619 million (40.3% of all private enterprises), per SAMR data. In foreign trade, their share rose from 39.7% in 2018 to 57.3% in 2025, and they provide over 80% of urban employment. The Private Economy Promotion Law took effect on May 20, 2025, reinforcing equal treatment and fair competition.
items.title: Chinese Private Enterprises Drive High-Quality Economic Growth

items.summary: The 2026 Light of the Internet Expo opened Monday in Wuzhen, Zhejiang Province, as a flagship event of the World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit. It showcased more than 1,000 new technologies and products from 671 companies across 54 countries, plus over 100 embodied intelligent robots for sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare and elderly care.
items.title: Satellite Internet, 6G and Robots Shine at Wuzhen Expo

items.summary: The Supreme Court of India responded sharply on Monday to a plea about steep airfare increases. Justice Vikram Nath told the counsel, "Don't travel by air," before moving on. The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter.
items.title: Supreme Court Judge Dismisses Plea Over Airfare Hike

items.summary: The BJP alleged a rift in Congress leadership, claiming Rahul Gandhi's camp was sidelining his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said she was denied speaking opportunities and seated second row during events on October 31. He offered no independent evidence to support these claims.
items.title: BJP Alleges Rift Between Gandhi Siblings Over Ramlila Rally Role

items.summary: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission approved tariffs discovered through competitive bidding for a 450 MW / 900 MWh standalone battery storage project in Gujarat. Allocated to NLC India Renewables Limited and Sun Drops Energia Limited under GUVNL's Phase-IX procurement, the projects follow an earlier developer failure to execute agreements. Supported by Viability Gap Funding, they aim to meet Energy Storage Obligations while strengthening grid stability.
items.title: GERC Approves Tariffs for Gujarat Battery Storage Projects

items.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visited China in October, arriving on the 27th before talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping that began around October 30. In Hefei he toured Volkswagen's largest research center outside Germany, where technologies were developed by a local joint venture for China's smart-auto market. Both leaders framed the trip as evidence of a shift from trade-focused ties toward innovation partnerships in artificial intelligence and green development. Steinmeier said dialogue could resolve trade differences while supporting free-trade rules; Xi called for cooperation based on equality and mutual benefit, describing it as an engine for broader China-EU relations.
items.title: China and Germany Chart Deeper Innovation Partnership

items.summary: Andy Burnham declined in an ITV interview to say net migration was too high, though he said small boat crossings were 'too high, for certain'. Shabana Mahmood will later announce tougher indefinite leave to remain rules requiring longer waits. The context has shifted as net migration falls and Reform UK's poll lead recedes.
items.title: Burnham declines net migration claim as Mahmood prepares settlement rules

items.summary: John Leeson, best known as the voice of the robot dog K9 in Doctor Who, has died at 83. His son Guy Ducker announced it after a summer of illness, describing an end that was peaceful. Colleagues remembered him for his distinctive performance and his work across stage, television and audio dramas.
items.title: John Leeson, voice of K9 in Doctor Who, dies aged 83

items.summary: A business jet crashed into a multi-lane road near Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people aboard. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the deaths and said the FAA was assisting an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board. Governor Ron DeSantis called the scene jarring, describing it as a missile coming down with a massive explosion.
items.title: Nine Killed When Business Jet Crashes Into Florida Street

items.summary: Ryanair is considering cost-cutting measures, including temporary pay freezes, lower crew ratios and greater use of AI, to offset soaring jet-fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict. Its own fuel bill could rise by about €2bn in its next financial year, ending March 2028. Chief executive Michael O’Leary said fares may increase materially but would not fully cover higher prices.
items.title: Ryanair weighs pay freezes and crew cuts as fuel costs surge

items.summary: Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff as it copes with sharply higher fuel costs driven by the US-Israel war with Iran. The carrier forecasts its short-term fuel bill to rise €2bn (£1.6bn) and says European airfares will increase, though it doubts that alone will cover bills. Pre-tax profits fell 16% to €2.4bn in the six months to end of September. CEO Michael O'Leary expects fares up 15% to 20% next year but warns they may not offset rising oil costs.
items.title: Ryanair weighs pay freeze and fare hikes over fuel surge

items.summary: Two days before Michigan’s midterm legislative elections, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed her progressive rival Abdul El‑Sayed’s opponent, Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. The move followed a dispute in which El‑Sayed said Stevens was no longer welcome at his campaign events and that she should “away.” Stevens posted the endorsement on X on November 1, 2026, after appearing with Mr. Rogers at a Detroit church event. U.S. President Donald Trump praised her decision as “bravery,” while several of her congressional office staffers resigned in response. El‑Sayed dismissed the drama, saying it did not matter to him.
items.title: Michigan Democrat Endorses Republican Rival Amid Party Rift

items.summary: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published a list identifying press freedom 'predators' for an interview marking the United Nations International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists. Thibaut Bruttin, RSF's Director General and Secretary-General, welcomed the occasion, stating that when journalists are killed it is everyone's right to know what is being endangered.
items.title: RSF Releases List of Press Freedom Predators Ahead of UN Day

items.summary: An EL PAÍS USA Edition article frames the upcoming November 3 U.S. midterm election as a referendum on whether Trumpism survives, describing Donald Trump's record-setting campaign tour dubbed 'Midterm Blitz,' which will have brought him to 28 rallies and about 60 hours of events by Election Day. The piece notes that Republicans trailed eight points in generic ballot polling before the summer and may lose the House while ceding the Senate remains a remote prospect. It presents early voting figures — just over 51 million citizens as of Saturday, which forecast high turnout — with two readings offered: one favoring Republican mobilization, another bolstering Democratic hopes. The article also examines Elon Musk's spending at least $267 million to support Republicans in the midterms compared with roughly $290 million for Trump's 2024 campaign, and notes his fortune grew by about $2.7 billion since returning to power.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Blitz Framed as a Referendum on Trumpism

items.summary: More companies in Japan are taking out cybersecurity insurance policies following several high-profile data breaches, including last week's attack on GMO Internet Group. Such incidents highlight the significant financial risk that cyberattacks pose to businesses. The coverage typically includes compensation for breach-related costs such as hacking and internal leaks, digital forensic analysis to identify attackers and system vulnerabilities, prevention assessments, and losses from missed business opportunities.
items.title: Japanese firms increase cybersecurity insurance after data breaches

items.summary: The U.N.'s peacekeeping mission for disputed Western Sahara, MINURSO, ceased operations on Sunday after 35 years amid a U.S.-Russia standoff over the territory's future. The secretary-general announced that 1 November 2026 marks the start of the liquidation period, with a smaller team overseeing asset disposal. Russia vetoed a draft resolution supporting Morocco and ended the mission next year; a rival Russian extension vote was also defeated. Morocco welcomed the non-renewal as an instrument to internationalize the dispute, while Algeria-backed Polisario called it unacceptable. The force had been authorized for 534 personnel with a budget of more than $62 million in 2026-2027.
items.title: UN Peacekeeping Mission in Western Sahara Ends After 35 Years

items.summary: The Bank of Japan said a shrinking population makes robust consumer-spending growth unlikely, warning weak aggregate consumption may not signal weaker household demand. The internal affairs ministry reported a 2.5% fall in 2025, the fastest since 1920. BNP Paribas and Daiichi Life Research Institute forecast Q3 GDP decline due Nov. 16.
items.title: Bank of Japan Cautions on Consumer Spending Amid Population Decline

items.summary: Micron Technology gave Boise $2.5 million in December to extend its geothermal heating system, the country’s largest, toward a planned affordable housing development with more than 300 units. The city says renewable heat could save residents up to 80% on utility bills and support Boise’s goal of becoming carbon-neutral by 2050.
items.title: Boise Expands Geothermal Network With Micron Funding

items.summary: Exclusive Grist polling from Data for Progress shows that about 58 percent of likely U.S. voters believe a warming climate will hinder their ability to achieve or maintain the American Dream over the next 20 years, including 42 percent of Republicans. The survey was conducted this spring with 1,167 likely voters and found cost of living as the top current threat, while only about 2 percent named climate change first. Grace Adcox of Data for Progress noted that voters may resist sacrifice framing despite Trump’s rhetoric linking his policies to the American Dream.
items.title: Poll Finds Voters See Climate Change as Threat to American Dream

items.summary: The Communist Party of China concluded its fifth plenary session in Beijing, adopting a resolution titled Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. The resolution stressed maintaining a tough stance against corruption and strengthening checks on power.
items.title: China's CPC Concludes Fifth Plenary Session on Party Self-Governance

items.summary: Kylian Mbappé apologised after a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong drew backlash in China. In a video, he said his favourite meme showed 'a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator', before an altered image placed his face on Mao's body. At least three Chinese companies ended brand deals with him, and CCTV pulled a Real Madrid match from its schedule.
items.title: Mbappé Apologises After Mao Meme Comment Sparks Chinese Backlash

items.summary: Germany's digital minister Karsten Wildberger confirmed that members of the Bundestag and federal government received warnings from Apple that their iPhones may have been targeted by mercenary spyware. The alerts began reaching affected phones on 29 October, per a Federal Office for Information Security letter seen by Wildberger. Those affected were told to treat their devices as compromised, though it remains unknown who is behind the attack or how many people were hit.
items.title: German officials warned iPhones targeted by spyware

items.summary: Pakistan’s Private Power and Infrastructure Board is seeking a consultant to support the development of 100 MW of distributed solar power plants in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Water and Power Department will execute the project, while the chosen consultant verifies non-solar works such as transmission lines and substations. Applications open with an expression of interest stage and are due November 30; international bidders may apply.
items.title: Pakistan Board Seeks Consultant for Distributed Solar Project

items.summary: A Brookings Institution report says the Department of Government Efficiency removed about $468 million from tribal programs, roughly half for environmental and natural resources. The cuts follow a 2025 cancellation by the Trump administration of an EPA wind-energy grant to Kotzebue, Alaska, that would have cut diesel reliance toward 40–50 percent. Brookings links the losses to One Big Beautiful Bill Act repeals of Inflation Reduction Act streams and flags historic Biden-era tribal funding at over $700 million as now defunded. Authors Rob Maxim and Glencora Haskins call for Congress to bar grant cancellation and route funds directly to tribes, citing trust obligations amid worsening climate disasters.
items.title: DOGE Cuts $468M in Tribal Climate Funding

items.summary: A one-year-old child died in a house fire in Western Australia's South West, with authorities investigating the cause. Firefighters extinguished the blaze at a home in Collie, about 200 kilometres south of Perth, on Sunday afternoon before the body was found. Police said several people were inside but escaped safely. A WA Police spokesperson said the death is not being treated as suspicious and that a coroner's report would be prepared.
items.title: One-Year-Old Dies in House Fire Near Perth

items.summary: Charities giving Christmas presents to struggling families say more children need help but donations are falling this year. Martyna Lee, founder of the Chard appeal started in 2019 from her living room, said families worry about affording gifts and have 'tears in their eyes'. She noted they receive more referrals and fewer donations due to cost of living. Gill Harrison of Christmas Sparkle in Taunton reported demand rising sharply over recent years - from 500 presents given out in 2015 to around 10,000 individual gifts last year - with possibly higher requests expected this year as the cost-of-living crisis continues.
items.title: Somerset charities report rising Christmas gift demand amid cost of living crisis

items.summary: A recent study confirms that the Bangka slow loris, declared possibly extinct on the IUCN Red List in 2015 after its last documented sighting around 1937, still survives. Researchers analyzed more than 90 lorises rescued by Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center and mapped 39 across four districts of Bangka Island in 2021, indicating wide distribution. Co-author Timon Glaw noted the species had been overlooked for nearly a century. The authors state it is not yet extinct and recommend reassessment, habitat protections, post-release tracking, and an ex-situ breeding program.
items.title: Rescued Primate Confirms Survival of Species Once Listed as Possibly Extinct

items.summary: A private Learjet 60 crashed Sunday in Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people aboard after nose-diving into a residential area and exploding. Air traffic control recordings show the pilots reporting turbulence, icing and precipitation before descent accelerated to up to 30,000 feet per minute — exceeding design limits. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation; cause and identities remain unknown.
items.title: Nine Killed When Learjet Crashes in South Florida Neighborhood

items.summary: The Geelong Cats finished second on percentage behind North Melbourne after becoming the highest-scoring regular-season AFLW team of all time, with a final score of 88 to 20. Co-captain Nina Morrison said their rise to premiership contenders “doesn't feel like it's come out of the blue.” The Cats face Melbourne in Saturday's qualifying final at Princes Park.
items.title: Geelong Cats surge into AFLW finals contention

items.summary: Friends and family mourn the death of TV actor Anuj Thakur, who died last week after a seizure during sleep. Casting director Rupesh Sonar shared tributes on Instagram, saying he had met Thakur just ten days earlier.
items.title: TV Actor Anuj Thakur Dies at 33 After Seizure in Sleep

items.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of forcibly shutting shops in Connaught Place on 1 November, ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. In a video shared on his social media account, he said traders had been told to shop during the march but found every single shop closed. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh later called fears about trader losses a smear campaign and thanked Delhi's business community for supporting the protest. Chamber of Trade & Industry chairman Brijesh Goyal estimated trading-sector losses at ₹10,000–11,000 crore, citing updates from traders' WhatsApp groups that said around 80% of shops stayed closed. BJP leaders, including JP Nadda and Amit Shah, echoed the concerns while criticising Congress for ignoring postponement requests during the festive season.
items.title: BJP Blamed for Delhi Shop Closures as Traders Warn of Festive Losses

items.summary: A retractable solar roof of 5,280 photovoltaic modules is under construction above the aeration tanks at Stuttgart-Mühlhausen’s main wastewater treatment plant. Stadtwerke Stuttgart says it will reach an installed capacity of 2.745 MW on completion in the second quarter of 2027, making it Germany’s largest retractable solar roof. The project uses Helioflex technology from dhp Technology and is expected to generate more than 2.2 GWh annually for on-site use.
items.title: Stuttgart Builds Germany’s Largest Retractable Solar Roof Over Wastewater Plant

items.summary: Senior Delhi journalist Ajaz Ashraf argues that Congress should boycott the February-MMarch 2027 State Assembly elections to pressure the Modi government into electoral reforms. Writing about Rahul Gandhi’s INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, where speakers targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, he frames a boycott as a principled stand rather than a gamble tied to election outcomes. Ashraf contends Congress alone has an all-India footprint and can bear the cost—Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa together account for just 20 Lok Sabha seats—drawing on historical precedents from 1937. He warns that winning could let BJP claim electoral fairness while losing would stall reforms.
items.title: Congress Should Boycott Assembly Elections To Defend Democracy

items.summary: M K Stalin and Thangam Thennarasu accused the ruling TVK government of driving Tamil Nadu into an economic downturn. Stalin cited GST revenue growth falling below India's national average of 22.9 per cent in October, plus a reported Rs 1,614-crore Korean investment proposal relocating to Andhra Pradesh. Thennarasu said Tamil Nadu's collections grew only 3 per cent versus 24 per cent for Andhra Pradesh, and contracted by 1 per cent in August and 5 per cent in September. Both leaders called on the government to boost domestic production.
items.title: DMK leaders blame Vijay government for Tamil Nadu's economic slowdown

items.summary: The Supreme Court refused urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly a 700 per cent rise in airfares, telling a petitioner on Monday not to travel by air. An advocate claimed fares had jumped that much and called aviation an essential service violating Article 14. The court is separately hearing S Laxminarayanan's petition for a robust regulator; the Centre said rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 are likely to be published soon. The article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
items.title: Supreme Court Tells Petitioner Not To Travel By Air Amid Fare Hike Plea

items.summary: Hidden-camera footage shows Punjab Police ASI Sukhdev Singh placing heroin under a mattress at Shiv Sena leader Mahant Kashmir Giri's Khanna residence. A police team then recovered around 30 grams of the drug, and Giri was arrested before being discharged from the case. The video prompted his suspension, an SIT probe, and political backlash as Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked the AAP government.
items.title: Punjab cop caught planting drugs at Sena leader's home

items.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara says Virat Kohli has a better chance than opener Rohit Sharma of scoring a century in the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand. He attributes this to Kohli’s number-three position, which suits an anchor role and gives him time to settle. Pujara also expects the series to be closely contested.
items.title: Kohli has better chance of scoring century than Rohit: Pujara drops big verdict

items.summary: Europe is preparing a digital battery passport required for e-bike batteries sold in the EU from February 18, 2027. The rule stems from the EU’s 2023 Batteries Regulation and covers cars, bicycles, scooters and other light electric vehicles. Scanning QR codes may reveal manufacturer, chemistry, capacity and carbon data, though some details could stay restricted to authorized users. Because many manufacturers sell in both regions, US riders might eventually benefit through spillover rather than a new American law.
items.title: EU Battery Passport May Reach US E-Bike Riders

items.summary: Author Parvathi Sajiv presents a book tracing Indian protest history from the freedom struggle through movements to the early 2020s, examining how they shaped laws and public discourse. She notes many protests took decades before prompting government action. Citing the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, she reports 110 anti-government protests worldwide in the last twelve months, with 31 active as of July 29, 2026, attributing them to governments’ anti-democratic actions. The book highlights India’s current resistance to the ₹44,000-crore Ken-Betwa Link Project and concludes that satyagraha remains a unifying thread in Indian protest. Excerpted with permission from Duckbill Publishing.
items.title: New Book Explores How Protests Shaped Laws in India

items.summary: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLAs from Punjab joined the Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday, ahead of Assembly elections expected early next year. Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jauramajra resigned Sunday; Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh followed that day. BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon called the AAP a “sinking ship” and said more resignations were expected, while AAP chief Aman Arora accused the BJP of gathering expelled leaders with no base in Punjab.
items.title: Three AAP MLAs Join BJP Ahead of Punjab Assembly Polls

items.summary: Turkish firm TAV Airports announced a second-phase investment of $353.9 million at Almaty Airport, raising its total in Kazakhstan to around $642.5 million. CEO Serkan Kaptan said the initial program completed in 2024 delivered new terminals. The airport nearly doubled passenger traffic to 11.9 million by 2025 and handled 9.47 million passengers through September this year, with international arrivals up 11%. TAV has operated it since 2021.
items.title: TAV Airports Expands Almaty Airport Investment Amid Türkiye-Kazakhstan Ties

items.summary: Vedanta Oil and Gas shares rose to Rs 31.90 on Monday, part of a two-day rally after the company reported consolidated net profit of Rs 746 crore for the second quarter of FY27, up from a Rs 91 crore loss a year earlier but down from Rs 945 crore in the first quarter. Revenue rose over 6% to Rs 2,488 crore and EBITDA jumped 34% YoY to Rs 1,393 crore.
items.title: Vedanta Oil and Gas Shares Jump After Q2 Profit

items.summary: Police say eight to ten men allegedly tampered with railway signalling to halt the Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express in Satara district, Maharashtra, and robbed three women passengers of gold ornaments worth around ₹2 lakh. The incident occurred near Salpa railway station around 2.30am on Sunday. Investigators are conducting a search operation while questions arise about security arrangements despite RPF presence.
items.title: Maharashtra Gang Robs Women Passengers of Gold on Trained Train

items.summary: GAIL reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 4,719.66 crore in Q2FY27, up 139.3% year-on-year to Rs 4,720 crore, with revenue from operations rising 32.7% YoY to Rs 47,301.03 crore. The company's board approved an initial public offering for its wholly owned subsidiary GAIL Gas Ltd, involving dilution of up to 25% of GAIL's equity stake, and cleared the transfer of six city gas distribution areas—Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum, Cuttack and Khordha—to that subsidiary. Shares gained about 4% on the results.
items.title: GAIL Shares Rise on Strong Q2 Profit and GAIL Gas IPO Approval

items.summary: On Monday, Russia and Ukraine exchanged accusations over cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems. Moscow reported a hack of its emergency alerts app hours after Kyiv said its own air raid warning system had been compromised. The incidents coincided with the expiry of a fragile ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region, raising fears of renewed fighting.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Trade Cyberattack Blame as Ceasefire Ends

items.summary: A few dozen right-wing activists gathered outside Gadi Eisenkot's residence in Herzliya to oppose the new Israeli-Arab coalition. Protester Viktor Shriki said the demonstration aimed to block a Palestinian state formed with Arab and Muslim groups. Netanyahu warned against what he called a dangerous government, noting Arab parties represent 20% of Israel's population, while Likud claimed Tuesday's election was stolen without providing evidence.
items.title: Right-wing activists protest Israeli-Arab coalition government plans

items.summary: NVIDIA introduces the open-source NVIDIA Workload Map, part of its DSX AI Factory Platform, which offers a shared description of Kubernetes workload structure so schedulers and platforms can interpret workloads without per-framework adapters. It ships prebuilt definitions for JobSet and other types and is used in production within NVIDIA Run:ai.
items.title: NVIDIA Launches Workload Map To Speed Up AI Framework Support

items.summary: On Monday, Versant's MS NOW announced it was expanding its direct-to-consumer membership to connected TV platforms for the first time, letting members watch its live feed on a TV without cable. The 24/7 feed launched November 2 across Roku, Apple TV, Samsung, Google TV and Amazon Fire TV at $7.99 monthly or $79.99 yearly.
items.title: Versant Expands MS NOW Membership to Connected TV

items.summary: City Union Bank announced on Monday that the Reserve Bank of India approved appointing Sankaran G, its current Executive President, as Whole-time Director (Executive Director) for a three-year term beginning when he assumes charge. The bank said it would take steps to induct him onto its Board and notify the stock exchange after approval.
items.title: RBI Approves City Union Bank Executive Director Appointment

items.summary: An amended SEC filing showed Anthropic's third-quarter net loss fell to $23.29 billion from $66.3 billion, while revenue rose to $16.96 billion from $11.56 billion. The San Francisco-based AI company filed to go public last week amid a lull in the IPO market driven by higher bond yields and rate-hike expectations.
items.title: Anthropic's Q3 Loss Shrinks as Revenue Jumps Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Trade unions are expected to expand access into UK big tech after new workplace rights came into force, with Prospect reaching an agreement with Google on Monday to organise among about 7,000 workers across its UK operations. The deal lets unions communicate with non-unionised staff and encourage membership. Meta signed a similar pact earlier; the TUC general secretary expects more recognition deals over the next year as the rules take effect.
items.title: UK Unions Gain Workplace Access at Google After Employment Rights Overhaul

items.summary: Federal prosecutors are demanding an action plan after authorities found cyanide-contaminated ponds in the Raposa Serra do Sol Indigenous Territory in Brazil's Roraima state. Illegal miners, who traditionally used mercury but increasingly turned to cheaper and more efficient cyanide as raids cut off its supply, have left behind contaminated water. The Federal Police arrested two men and seized about 375 kilograms of a chemical compound consistent with cyanide. IBAMA says the presence of cyanide does not prove smuggling and requires further testing before it can determine whether legally authorized sales were diverted.
items.title: Prosecutors demand cleanup plan as illegal cyanide mining poisons Amazon Indigenous land

items.summary: According to a report by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple plans an upgraded entry-level iPad and refreshed iPad Air with OLED display plus faster iPad Pro in the first half of 2027. The refresh follows recent iPad mini revamp amid wider product push including iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro lineup launches.
items.title: Apple Aims for Major iPad Refresh in Early 2027

items.summary: Microsoft priced a $25 billion bond sale, its first US investment-grade offering since 2017, three days after offering voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees. CFO Amy Hood said the company has not yet tapped debt markets given its ratings. The proceeds fund general corporate purposes and capital expenditure as AI data centre bills climb. Orders peaked at $115 billion; the sale closes November 4. Microsoft expects 3,000 or fewer takers of the exit offer.
items.title: Microsoft Funds AI Spending With Bond Sale and Staff Buyouts

items.summary: AI company Anthropic reported nearly $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, about 12 times the prior-year figure, per a Monday filing. Its net loss widened to $23.3 billion from $12.1 billion last year, and operating expenses rose 292% to $17.5 billion. Anthropic filed an amended prospectus with the SEC on Monday under ticker ANT, aiming for a debut that could rival SpaceX's market launch.
items.title: Anthropic's revenue jumps as it prepares Nasdaq IPO

items.summary: Economist Jeffrey D. Sachs praised the Adani Group as a primary driver of India's infrastructure-led growth, speaking at The World Symposium in Varanasi on Monday. He emphasized that family-run business models advance social responsibility and highlighted the conglomerate's work through its foundation. Sachs also referenced Unilever CEO Paul Polman to illustrate challenges embedding corporate responsibility amid shareholder pressure.
items.title: Sachs Credits Adani Group for India's Infrastructure Growth

items.summary: On Monday, OpenAI signed four agreements with Abu Dhabi-based entities to deploy artificial intelligence across the emirate’s oil industry, government services and investment operations, per the Abu Dhabi Media Office. The signing was witnessed by Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan after meeting CEO Sam Altman. Deals include ADNOC using AI for oilfield planning via G42's Inception42, a food-imports pilot at the Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, Mubadala analyzing investments with OpenAI, and a five-year UAE-wide adoption agreement.
items.title: OpenAI Signs Four Abu Dhabi Deals Across Energy, Government and Investment

items.summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) are providing a combined €60 million to finance a 246 MW / 512.5 MWh battery energy storage system at Tenevo in south-eastern Bulgaria, split between a €30 million EBRD loan and parallel RBI funding. Developed by Tenevo Solar Technologies, the facility will expand existing storage capacity alongside an established solar plant to support grid stability and renewable integration as Bulgaria grows its battery fleet.
items.title: EBRD and RBI Finance Large Battery Storage Project in Bulgaria

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is in Abu Dhabi, where he secured contracts to deploy AI products across government, the oil sector, and sovereign wealth management. The deals come as OpenAI reportedly seeks a large funding round ahead of an IPO delayed earlier this year. No financial terms were disclosed. A consortium including Mubadala-backed MGX may be the largest investor in the round.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Secures AI Contracts in Abu Dhabi Amid IPO Push

items.summary: OpenAI is preparing to merge the Chat and Work tabs in its ChatGPT desktop app, according to an email sent to users. The change lets a project move from exploration through completion in one place, while bringing files and plugins together. Codex stays separate but will share tokens with ChatGPT from the same allowance pool. OpenAI said most users would be unaffected.
items.title: OpenAI Merging ChatGPT Chat and Work Tabs Into One Screen

items.summary: Congress leaders reached Delhi on Monday to file a petition challenging approvals for the proposed Google data centre in Visakhapatnam. APCC vice-president Vegi Venkatesh, Congress president Hasini Varma and senior advocate Krishna called for a review of environmental clearances, water usage and community impact. They seek a stay on construction and said development should not come at the cost of natural resources.
items.title: Congress Leaders Challenge Google Data Centre in Supreme Court

items.summary: Apple is set to report its first quarterly results since John Ternus took over from Tim Cook in September, with the Monday evening figures due. Investors focus on Christmas-quarter guidance amid uncertainty about demand for the foldable iPhone Duo and how Apple handles rising memory-chip costs that pushed component prices up sharply. Analysts at AJ Bell expect revenue growth of nearly 11% to $113.39 billion (€101.5bn) and net profit gains of about 6%, while noting Apple's restrained AI spending contrasts with rivals' heavy investment.
items.title: Apple's new CEO faces earnings test as rising chip costs cloud outlook

items.summary: Microsoft resolved an issue that blocked some users from activating Smart App Control after installing the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 security update. The company said devices running Windows 11 24H2 and later could not toggle the feature on, leaving them unprotected against harmful apps unless it was already enabled. On Wednesday Microsoft confirmed the fix ships in preview update KB5127936, released October 28, 2026 and later. It also offered a registry-based workaround for admins who prefer to wait for next month's Patch Tuesday updates.
items.title: Microsoft patches Smart App Control activation break from October Windows update

items.summary: Chinese regulators announced a set of support measures on Nov 2, following an 8.5% slump in the CSI300 Index during October, its worst month since early 2016. The People's Bank of China said swap operations could inject more than 100 billion yuan into markets and would convert a temporary buyback lending scheme to long-term at a rate cut to 1%. It urged index firms and tech companies to support share prices as confidence weakened amid property debt and sluggish consumption.
items.title: China deploys measures to stabilise struggling stock markets

items.summary: Google's parent company Alphabet launched its second euro bond sale this year, testing a debt market that is growing wary of the artificial intelligence trade. The issuance arrives as investors approach borrowing limits: Morgan Stanley said AI-related lending ballooned to almost $500 billion through September, up from $100 billion in the same period last year. An expert noted the boom may not be large enough to overcome high interest rates.
items.title: Alphabet Issues Second Eurobond Amid AI Debt Concerns

items.summary: Shares of Reliance Industries (RIL) rose 11.6% to close at Rs 1,300 on the NSE on Monday, their largest single-day gain since April 2020 per Bloomberg data. The rise lifted RIL's market capitalisation by around Rs 1.83 lakh crore toward Rs 17.6 lakh crore as its parent reported a 40.64% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 25,548 crore for Q2 FY27 versus Rs 18,165 crore a year earlier.
items.title: Reliance Shares Hit Biggest Single-Day Gain Since April 2020 on Strong Profit Report

items.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology released a lay-language cybersecurity guide, NIST Cybersecurity White Paper 50 (Small Business Cybersecurity: Non-Employer Firms), aimed at solopreneurs — businesses with one paid employee. The publication updates the earlier Small Business Information Security: The Fundamentals (NISTIR 7621) and draws on CSF 2. 0, offering actionable best practices such as data backups and updated software for busy solo business owners with limited technical knowledge or budget. NIST author Daniel Eliot said it provides a starting point rather than comprehensive coverage for every reader's needs. The article notes more than 28 million small businesses in the U. S.
items.title: NIST Releases Cybersecurity Guide for Solopreneurs and Small Non-Employer Firms

items.summary: Tata Motors began November with a sales milestone, selling 75,426 passenger vehicles across domestic and international markets in October 2026 versus 61,295 units the prior year. Its electric vehicle business posted the standout result: 16,244 EVs against 9,286 a year earlier, a 75% jump that the item frames as possibly reshaping India's competitive EV market.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Sharp Rise in October EV Sales

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani became the world's largest billionaire wealth gainer, adding USD 6.3 billion to his fortune as reported by Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list update of November 2. The gain followed a 40.6 per cent rise in Reliance Industries consolidated net profit to Rs 25,548 crore for the September quarter, driven by refining and Jio gains. Ambani rose to No.23 on the ranking, ahead of Gautam Adani at No.26 with USD 79.12 billion.
items.title: Ambani Tops Global Billionaire Wealth Gainers on Reliance Earnings Beat

items.summary: A Singapore Economic Development Board survey released on Nov 2 found a net weighted balance of 24% of manufacturers expect better business conditions between October 2026 and March 2027, up from 12% previously. Optimism is tied to AI demand, though firms cite overseas price competition and geopolitical factors as export risks. Electronics (+55%) and precision engineering lead on output expectations; chemicals (-13%) are most pessimistic. The survey covered 397 establishments surveyed with an 83% response rate.
items.title: Singapore Manufacturers See Strong AI-Driven Demand Through Next Six Months

items.summary: The European Union and Canada announced a broad package of digital cooperation after signing an agreement on Oct. 30, as reported by Tech Policy Press's Mark Scott on Nov. 2, 2026. The bloc signed the deal with Ottawa while Washington’s ties to both allies deteriorated, though neither side explicitly referenced the US in its communiqué. Proposals include a digital trade pact covering cross-border data flows and regulatory cooperation, AI infrastructure investment, high-performance computing membership, mutual recognition of digital identities, cybersecurity arrangements, election-integrity safeguards ahead of 2027 elections, and expanded internet subsea cable connectivity. Bilateral digital-services trade reached almost €20 billion in 2025 per the European Commission. Most commitments remain proposals; only three had moved beyond that stage. The relationship still requires large infrastructure investment and shared standards to mature.
items.title: EU and Canada Advance Digital Partnership Amid Strained US Relations

items.summary: Cole Donovan argues that several assertions made by OSTP director Michael Kratsios in a New York Times interview deserve scrutiny. He accepts the premise that scientific breakthroughs are slowing but contests its framing, noting federal R&D spending is dominated by defense development rather than basic research and that private funding already supplies roughly three-quarters of total R&D dollars. Donovan points to NIH grant success rates around one in five as evidence against a simple slowdown narrative, and he highlights concerns about the R&D tax credit directing billions toward large firms and AI infrastructure. He contends existing oversight mechanisms are adequate while warning that redirecting resources could undermine research quality, concluding that policy debates should reflect the full private-sector-weighted ecosystem rather than idealized basic-research models.
items.title: An economist disputes White House science-policy claims

items.summary: Jain and Kothari argue that poor customers' limited purchasing power keeps many firms small in India beyond regulatory distortions. In the US only 2% of manufacturing workers are in five-or-fewer-person firms versus nearly 60% in India; within India's richest states about 40% work there, against almost 90% in its poorest (Figure 1). Their research shows richer households pay more for identical goods and larger firms charge more, certify ISO or export. A calibrated model attributes up to around 40% of the cross-state firm-size gap to rising incomes shifting demand toward higher-quality goods made at scale; small-firm employment fell from 77% in 1989 to 58% in 2009 and the model reproduces about two-thirds. The authors treat these figures as upper bounds, since regulation and credit channels are set aside (s42). They recommend interventions on demand and capability rather than size alone (s46-47).
items.title: Affordability, Not Just Regulation, Keeps Indian Firms Small

items.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple plans three new iPad models—iPad Air, iPad Pro, and an entry-level iPad—in the first half of 2027. The iPad Air would gain an OLED display and M5 chip; the Pro a vapor chamber cooling system and possibly the M6 or M7 chip; the entry-level model would add Apple Intelligence support via 8GB RAM and the A19 chip, with no display or design upgrades expected.
items.title: Apple Set for Three New iPads in Early 2027

items.summary: Three deaths followed mobile-phone arguments in Surat's Kosad and Nanpura areas. A 22-year-old woman was arrested for allegedly stabbing her father after he smashed her phone during a gaming dispute; police registered a murder case on his wife's complaint. Elsewhere, two 17-year-olds were reportedly stabbed to death over an argument about horse-racing videos shared in a WhatsApp group named 'Salman Khan.' Police took three teenagers into custody.
items.title: Two phone and WhatsApp disputes in Surat turned fatal, killing three people.

items.summary: Sergio Correia, Emil Verner and Stephan Luck of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York present a staff report on how banking supervision identifies and disciplines failing banks. They argue closures stem from supervisory decisions based on hard information about book equity, which itself is partly produced by supervisors requiring troubled banks to recognize losses. Their analysis uses examination data covering commercial bank failures from 2000 to 2023. Stricter supervision can lower resolution costs but may tighten credit supply when conditions are weak. The authors note their findings are positive and draw no normative conclusions about optimal strictness.
items.title: Fed Economists Find Supervisors Shape Bank Failures Through Hard Information and Trade-Offs

items.summary: Bill Tan raised concern that aluminium road dividers may not protect drivers as well as steel guard rails, following two recent accidents in Tampines. He noted several years ago a driver died at the junction of Tampines Avenue 10 and Tampines Avenue 1 (Dec 25, 2021). An accident along Tampines Avenue 12 recently claimed two lives. Tan argued that dividers should provide effective run-off and impact protection at bends and major junctions.
items.title: Aluminium road dividers questioned after fatal Tampines crashes

items.summary: Francis Chu, a lawmaker, calls for balanced enforcement of road safety laws after a fatal crash in Tampines killed a motorcyclist and his pregnant wife. He cites rising speeding violations—201,358 in 2024, 253,550 in 2025, and 126,976 in the first half of 2026—and argues enforcement is uneven toward vulnerable road users like cyclists. He urges stronger consequences for hit-and-run offences.
items.title: Lawmaker Calls for Balanced Road Safety Enforcement After Tampines Crash

items.summary: Butaeva, Durlauf and Rudenko analyze Russian income data from Soviet collapse through 2025. Their harmonized household surveys show the Gini coefficient fell from about 0.45–0.48 in the early 2000s to 0.29–0.38 by the early 2020s, matching survey-based literature rather than official statistics.
items.title: Russian Income Inequality Fell After Rising in the 1990s, New Study Finds

items.summary: Jesús Fernández-Villaverde argues in NBER Working Paper 35964 (2026) that capital supply governs the size of automation's growth boom, while task structure sets its duration and wage evolution. He documents how a technology path yielding 11.7% annual growth with optimal saving delivers only 2.2% at the U.S. 2025 level of 23%, suggesting slow growth reflects insufficient capital accumulation rather than technological limits.
items.title: Saving for the Machines Explains Slow Growth Through Capital Accumulation

items.summary: The Indian government has moved to resolve a dispute over bulk Scotch whisky imports under the UK trade pact, assuring liquor companies that such shipments qualify for reduced 75 percent import duty after tax officials questioned their eligibility. According to Reuters citing six sources, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said steps were being taken so the concession would not be impaired. The disagreement stems from a CETA provision reducing duty from 150 per cent to 75 percent; officials argued bulk-container imports did not qualify, though around 80 percent of Scotch arrives in bulk.
items.title: India Moves to Resolve Scotch Whisky Tariff Dispute, Assures 75% Duty on Bulk Imports

items.summary: The Nationalist Congress Party dismissed reports of an internal rift after Union Home Minister Amit Shah met a delegation without deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons. Spokesperson Umesh Patil called the claims incorrect, baseless and misleading, saying attempts were made to create a false narrative of division. He urged media to verify information before reporting.
items.title: NCP Rejects Rift Rumours as Sunetra Pawar Skips Amit Shah Meeting

items.summary: The European Commission launched a WTO safeguard investigation into certain new hybrid vehicles, notifying that it is examining whether rising imports may cause or threaten serious injury to the Union industry. The Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security will collect questionnaire replies from producers, importers and dealers within 21 days of publication and invites interested parties to submit written views and evidence in the same period. A safeguard action can be taken only if increased imports are found to be causing or threatening serious injury (s0-s6).
items.title: EU Opens Safeguard Probe Into New Hybrid Vehicles

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department says Cyclone Murasu has intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of Tuesday, with landfall south of Ongole between 11:30 pm Monday and 4 am Tuesday. Winds could reach up to 120 kmph, bringing extremely heavy rainfall and coastal flooding risk.
items.title: Cyclone Murasu Set for Andhra Landfall Tonight with Heavy Winds and Rain

items.summary: CleanTechnica argues that Elon Musk is spending millions supporting Republican candidates amid a coordinated anti-transgender campaign strategy. The outlet cites US Federal Election Commission data showing Musk donated at least $445 million to Republican-aligned political action committees and groups since last year, with his donations concentrated in races like Texas's Senate contest for Ken Paxton against James Talerico. CleanTechnica attributes the broader strategy largely to Republican lawmakers while noting some Democratic involvement. The article frames Musk's spending as politically ineffective so far, quoting journalist Judd Legum on false ads and citing Carolyn Fortuna on growing condemnation of his election interference claims.
items.title: Elon Musk's Election Spending Draws Backlash Over Transgender Rights

items.summary: The Central Government has warned airlines that it retains authority to cap airfares during extraordinary situations under updated regulations applying from 2027. The rules also require tariff breakdowns at booking and prohibit hidden costs. Experts question the measures because they fail to define what counts as an extraordinary situation, limiting their practical impact despite reports of steep festive-season fare increases.
items.title: Centre Reserves Power To Cap Airfares In Extraordinary Situations, Mandates Complete Tariff Breakup

items.summary: Researchers propose an online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications, decoupling a Planning agent from a UI Grounding model and using LLM-as-a-Judge reward signals with Proximal Policy Optimization. Their 8B RL agents reportedly achieve nearly sevenfold improvement over supervised fine-tuning baselines in out-of-distribution Android generalization while accelerating convergence.
items.title: Online RL Agent Navigates Live iOS Apps

items.summary: Beijing’s newest export controls target construction equipment such as tunnel-boring machines, some of the world’s largest and most complex industrial devices. China dominates the global market at around 70%, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan said, a grip that raises dependency risks and may push other countries to de-risk from it. For India, which is building railways and roads near its disputed Himalayan border, controls could slow strategic projects but also strengthen its case as an alternative manufacturing base; Herrenknecht’s equipment maker noted foreign makers have incentive to add capacity in large markets like India. Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari said India aims to invest up to $9. 6 billion on tunneling over the next five years, while the government reportedly considers a $1. 2 billion incentive plan for construction-equipment makers. Larsen & Toubro president R.
items.title: China Adds Tunnel-Boring Machines to Export Controls, India Weighs Response

items.summary: Xia Lu, a CGTN special commentator and professor at Renmin University of China, argues that the Fifth Plenary Session's focus on comprehensive and rigorous self-governance strengthens public service delivery. She contends that disciplined grassroots organizations improve education equity through teacher rotations, healthcare via compact medical communities, and elderly care by curbing corruption in subsidies. Citing Beijing's complaint-response mechanism handling over 200 million cases with a satisfaction rate exceeding 97%, she frames strict Party discipline as an investment benefiting roughly 1.4 billion citizens rather than internal politics. The piece notes the author's views may not reflect CGTN's editorial stance and offers contact details for contributors.
items.title: CGTN Commentator Links Party Discipline to Public Welfare in China

items.summary: A wave of supermarket fridge and freezer hacks has affected more than 100 stores across Europe, AFP reports. Chains including SuperValu, Carrefour, Coop and Delhaize say cooling systems were tampered with overnight, forcing them to discard spoiled food; some losses ran into tens of thousands of euros. The EU's agriculture commissioner called it a deliberate attempt to disrupt the bloc's food supply.
items.title: Ikea among shops hit by European fridge cyber-hacks

items.summary: Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign reported a single-day fundraising record of $2.4m on Sunday, the same day Haley Stevens pulled her endorsement and backed Republican Mike Rogers. His staff said more than 26,000 people contributed for the first time; Politico separately reported that his campaign raised $1.2m in the four hours after Stevens defected. El-Sayed leads by 11 percentage points outside the margin of error in a race Democrats view as vital to retaining Senate control.
items.title: El-Sayed hits record fundraising day as Stevens endorses Rogers in Michigan Senate race

items.summary: The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity concluded in Yerevan, Armenia, after negotiators agreed its main decisions, including the Yerevan Pathway aimed at accelerating global biodiversity action. Held halfway between the adoption and 2030 deadline of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, whose review warned that targets would not be met without faster implementation, the pathway focuses on strengthening efforts to meet existing commitments rather than setting new ones. Nearly $2 billion in new funding was announced by the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity, alongside a report finding developed countries had failed to provide at least $20 billion annually as promised for 2025. Officials said the next four years will determine whether governments can turn commitments into measurable progress before the deadline. As Schomaker put it: "Ultimately, the test is not what governments agreed in Yerevan, but what they change when they return home."
items.title: COP17 Concludes With Yerevan Pathway for Biodiversity Action

items.summary: Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries reported overnight temperature surges across dozens of stores, with several firms confirming victims of a cyber-attack. Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden said their refrigeration systems failed around 2am; Sabcobel's Stephan Moelans described mobilising technicians at 1am to disconnect affected units. The incidents follow last month's French attack on up to 700 supermarkets supplied by Danfoss controllers, which caused fires, food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros and individual losses from tens of thousands to over €130,000 (£109,000). Authorities fear state-sponsored hybrid attacks amid Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The Paris prosecutor has opened an investigation into France; no one claims responsibility for the new incidents.
items.title: European supermarkets hit by second suspected cyber-attack on refrigeration systems

items.summary: In a Guardian opinion piece, Judd Legum argues that dark money from tech billionaires and corporate interests is distorting the 2026 midterms. He notes federal election spending rose from $3.8bn in 2014 to $8.9bn in 2022, with the Brennan Center estimating about $1.3bn in dark money already deployed this cycle. Legum contends that requiring Super Pacs and groups to disclose top donors would blunt attack ads' impact, citing academic studies from over the last 15 years and a 2024 Ninth Circuit ruling upholding Alaska's disclosure law. He promotes his app Paid For By as a tool for voters to identify ad funders, arguing that public pressure is needed since politicians benefit from the current system.
items.title: Judd Legum Proposes Reforms to Combat Dark Money in Elections

items.summary: Dozens of supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers. Around 40 Delhaize stores were affected while smaller numbers elsewhere reported incidents. Sabcobel, which manufactures some units and operates Delhaize's systems, said evaporators switched to defrost mode caused warming, possibly the same method as last month's French attack. CEO Stephan Moelans told Belga that teams worked overnight disconnecting units from the network. Freezer temperatures reportedly rose to 50C (122F). It is unclear who is behind it; Belgium and Sweden monitor the case while US authorities investigate a similar August incident at military bases.
items.title: Cyber-attack disrupts supermarket freezers across seven European countries

items.summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas added recently released export figures from its Database of Global Economic Indicators, covering April 1981 to August 2026. The graph tracks year-over-year growth in goods exported by the US, other advanced economies, emerging markets, and the world excluding the US. It shows that exports rise and fall together worldwide, swinging more than GDP—dropping as much as 34.6% during the Great Recession—and are measured in dollars deflated by US prices, which shapes how they appear.
items.title: Dallas Fed data show global merchandise exports swing widely

items.summary: A study by researchers at the Central University of Jammu has mapped potential foot-and-mouth disease risk zones where livestock migration routes overlap with protected areas across 15 of Jammu and Kashmir's 48 protected sites. Published July 2026, it used GIS analysis to identify 34 interfaces concentrated in Baramulla, Bandipora, Rajouri and Ganderbal. The authors note transmission has not been confirmed but highlight spillover risk to endangered species like the hangul and markhor. Experts caution that proximity alone cannot prove active spread.
items.title: Study Maps FMD Risk Zones in Jammu and Kashmir Wildlife Areas

items.summary: A Wizz Air passenger flight from London Luton Airport to Sofia was escorted by a Hungarian Gripen fighter jet and made an emergency landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International airport following a mid-air bomb threat. Authorities carried out security checks on the aircraft and passengers, which were completed with nothing found. The airline said it would depart again shortly while cooperating fully with authorities.
items.title: Hungarian fighter jet escorts Wizz Air flight after bomb threat

items.summary: DW outlines eight key factors that could tip the balance between war and peace in the ongoing conflict with Iran. The analysis draws on interviews with three analysts: Omid Memarian of DAWN, Leila Morovati, and Babak Rezaei Daryakenari of Leiden University. Factors include a possible Democratic victory in the US midterms, political deadlock in Israel's October 27 election, the nuclear impasse between Washington and Tehran, Iran's leverage over energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi actions in Yemen, regional mediators with stakes in resolution, Trump administration strategy after the November vote, and mounting economic pressure as the war enters its ninth month.
items.title: Eight factors shaping Iran war outcome amid US midterms

items.summary: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026 finds India's greenhouse gas emissions broke from rapid growth in 2025. Datasets disagree on the direction: EDGAR and IEA indicate a slight decline while the Energy Institute estimates a marginal increase. Renewable electricity generation rose about 98 terawatt-hours, nearly twice demand growth of 49 TWh, as coal-fired generation fell by 44 TWh. Milder weather also reduced cooling demand. Researchers caution sustained reductions need more investment in storage, transmission and industrial decarbonisation; whether the decline endures remains uncertain over a few years.
items.title: India's Emissions Slow as Renewables Displace Coal, UNEP Report Finds

items.summary: Ahead of the 2026 US midterms, Gen Z readers shared their concerns with the Guardian as young voters mobilize around the country's future. Nearly 50 million Americans aged 18 to 29 are eligible, though almost half remain unregistered or disengaged per US Census Bureau data. Readers cited rising living costs, immigration enforcement and ICE presence at polling locations, climate change, election integrity fears reminiscent of January 6, healthcare affordability, wealth inequality, artificial intelligence, LGBTQ+ rights and distrust in both parties. Tyler of Minnesota flagged inflation amid what he called an illegal war; Matthew Doutt of Tennessee expected ICE intimidation despite conservative gerrymandering; Scott warned Democrats lack a unifying vision while Connor Long feared Democratic underperformance under Trump.
items.title: Gen Z readers weigh in on midterms amid ICE, inflation and Trump

items.summary: Steve Smith, who founded Poundland and left it in 2006, has said he would invest again after being surprised to learn its current owners Gordon Brothers had filed for administration while sales rose 11% on the year. Business Minister Kate Dearden is understood to meet senior executives later this week about the threatened collapse of a business with up to 12,000 staff at risk and over 10,000 jobs in question. The meeting will be predominantly fact finding, with government sources conceding limited scope for intervention.
items.title: Poundland's former owner offers investment as minister meets board over insolvency

items.summary: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said cyberattacks targeted their emergency alert mobile apps, with Ukrainian users receiving false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat. Moscow reported that hackers gained access to the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry's app while efforts continued to restore its functionality.
items.title: Ukraine and Russia Report Fake Emergency Alerts After Cyberattacks Target Apps

items.summary: According to a confidential European Commission document obtained by Euronews, Kyiv is expected to transfer up to €1bn of Ukraine Support Loan funds into the European Defence Industry Programme / Ukraine Support Instrument. The move would more than quadruple the instrument’s current value and focus on air and missile defence, drones, counter-drone systems and ammunition as part of a broader EU-Ukraine partnership being formalised through a Defence Industrial Pact due by year-end 2026.
items.title: Ukraine Redirects Up To €1bn of EU Loan Into Joint Defence Projects

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department says severe cyclonic storm Murasu will likely make landfall on south Andhra Pradesh's coast between Nellore and Narsapur around midnight Monday as a 100-110 kmph storm, gusting to 120 kmph. It warns of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema over the next three days.
items.title: IMD Warns Cyclone Murasu Will Bring Heavy Rainfall Across Southern States

items.summary: A camera-trapping study in a protected area in northern Laos found that community-led ecotourism reduces localized hunting pressure but also scares wildlife away from areas near tourism routes. Researchers recorded an average of 4.58 species close to trekking and kayaking trails, with almost twice as many farther away. Lead author William Bleisch noted animals appear unable to distinguish tourists from hunters. Reviewer Paul Ouboter cautioned against treating tourism as a greater threat than hunting, logging or mining, while highlighting its conservation benefits. Further work is needed to understand the underlying causes of wildlife avoidance.
items.title: Laos Study Finds Ecotourism May Deter Hunters But Also Wildlife

items.summary: Delhi-NCR has been placed under Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan after air quality entered the “Very Poor” category, with the AQI touching 324 on November 2. The Commission for Air Quality Management brought the measures into force immediately, asking agencies to intensify efforts to curb pollution. Restrictions include barring non-BS-VI petrol and diesel vehicles registered outside Delhi from entering until January 31, 2027; prohibiting coal and firewood use in generators, homes and eateries; restricting diesel generator sets except for emergency services; routing trucks through peripheral expressways; halting construction at directed sites; and continuing road sweeping and water sprinkling. Authorities may also raise parking charges and stagger office timings. CAQM advised commuters to favour public transport.
items.title: Delhi Places Delhi-NCR Under GRAP Stage II Amid Very Poor Air

items.summary: The Oura Ring, a discreet titanium wearable worn on the finger, is part of a growing trend toward screenless health trackers that emphasize invisible performance and recovery over visible data. Unlike bulky smartwatches such as Apple Watch and Garmin, these devices track metrics like heart rate variability silently and deliver insights only when consulted. The current Oura Ring 5 costs €429 to €529 ($481 to $593) plus a subscription fee. High-profile athletes including Carlos Alcaraz use competing brands such as Whoop. Although the Finnish company founded in 2013 filed for an IPO with revenue above $1.2 billion and a valuation near $16 billion, its board postponed the offering in late September over market uncertainty. CEO Tom Hale describes the product as empowering users to manage their own health.
items.title: Oura Ring Leads Rise of Discreet Screenless Health Trackers

items.summary: Andrea R. Flores, a former White House and Department of Homeland Security official from Las Cruces, New Mexico, argues that the Democratic Party is a decade behind in developing an immigration answer. She contends Trump’s policies are the most extreme in modern American history because existing laws permit them, while noting border crossings have fallen sharply under his term. Flores warns Democrats lack their own alternative and would make a fatal mistake by failing to build one before taking over another White House. She advocates piecemeal legalization vehicles rather than comprehensive reform, citing concerns about leaving out portions of the undocumented population. The piece frames her views as opinion within an interview format published by EL PAÍS USA Edition.
items.title: Flores Urges Democrats on Immigration Reform

items.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won his fourth presidential term by defeating Jair Bolsonaro's son, Flávio Bolsonaro, on October 25, 2026. After trailing with 45.2 per cent of the first-round vote to Flávio Bolsonaro's 47 per cent, Lula engineered a turnaround and finished with 51.79 per cent to 48.21 per cent in the run-off. The shift followed his campaign pivot toward debt relief and a shorter working week after conceding "the most disorganised campaign in history." Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil two days later, reportedly using travel arrangements offered by Trump's administration. Lula framed the contest around sovereignty amid US tariffs and court pressure; climate activist Claudio Angelo called the result "the only thing standing between us and a wide destruction of the Amazon." The victory came as the opposition Liberal Party strengthened in Congress, leaving Lula to govern with a more independent central bank and a fractious legislature.
items.title: Lula Defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil Run-off

items.summary: The opposition INDIA coalition held a “Chalo Dilli” protest rally at the Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi promised legal action against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. He asserted that 13.3 crore votes were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision and claimed 15 per cent of voters had been removed, calling the 2024 Lok Sabha election a “stolen election,” noting only a 3 per cent margin between the NDA and INDIA blocs. The ruling BJP dismissed the event and questioned attendance figures. Analysts observe that while unity is emerging among opposition parties ahead of elections in states like Uttar Pradesh, translating this momentum into broader electoral success remains uncertain.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Ramlila Maidan Rally Opens New Road for Opposition

items.summary: Singapore-based Equator Renewables Asia introduced SolarBox, a containerized solar power system for industrial and temporary sites. The 235 kW to 250 kW unit fits in one shipping container and unfolds to about 120 meters, deploying in under three hours with two people. CEO Frank Phuan said it suits land available only briefly. ERA gave indicative LCOE estimates of $0.0194/kWh in Australia to $0.0292/kWh in Singapore, based on Q3 2026 equipment costs and excluding installation. The company has not disclosed a price or deployment timeline but signed an MOU with Aster Power for feasibility studies at facilities on Bukom and Jurong islands.
items.title: Equator Renewables Asia Launches Containerized SolarBox System

items.summary: Nearly 3,000 stone tools excavated from beneath Cairo more than a century ago show that specialised work was already reshaping village life before Egypt became a state. The Italian Egyptologist Ernesto Schiaparelli dug almost 9 metres down in 1905 and 1906 but kept the flints for monuments, so they sat forgotten in 40 wooden boxes at Turin's Museo Egizio until recent study. Researchers went through every box, assigning almost 3,000 objects to Heliopolis by cross-checking labels against Schiaparelli's notes and fingerprinting the flint with microscope and chemical analyses. The cores outnumbered blades, indicating a workshop producing more than its knappers needed while expert farmers relied on specialists for tools. This suggests early states built economic complexity on arrangements ordinary villagers had already worked out rather than inventing it from scratch.
items.title: Forgotten Heliopolis flints reveal early Egyptian craft specialisation

items.summary: A sociologist researching water service delivery in Madibeng's Damonsville, Mothutlung and Mmakau communities found that residents blame corruption and neglect rather than broken infrastructure for ongoing water failures. Interviews revealed residents judged the municipality on poor management, selective neglect and unfair tanker distribution, with some linking tap water to illness. The researcher noted official explanations focused on technical causes like ageing pipes and skills shortages. However, she clarified none of this proves misconduct: her research does not treat residents' claims as verified fact. Instead it documents how repeated institutional failure shapes trust between communities and the municipality over decades of poor service.
items.title: Residents Blame Corruption, Not Just Broken Pipes

items.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers less than 48 hours before Election Day, breaking with her party amid deteriorating relations with Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed and staff departures. Separately, NPR reports that after tomorrow's elections Trump may consider bombing Iran again — an option he has discussed with Israel — as Gulf states brace for potential conflict; Qatar led negotiations over the past 72 hours to prevent further fighting. The newsletter also previews a Supreme Court case on religious schools in Colorado pre-K programs and an NPR series on high-functioning depression.
items.title: Stevens Endorses Rogers; Gulf States Brace for Iran Attack

items.summary: Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the July-September quarter, with much of its net loss from non-cash valuation charges. Its amended IPO filing disclosed spending commitments of approximately $895 billion toward computing infrastructure, including $70 billion due before September 2027. The company is considering raising around $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion as it tests investor appetite for AI investments.
items.title: Anthropic's Revenue Surge and AI Spending Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Databricks announced that Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud, letting teams run serverless, production-grade PostgreSQL directly within its Data + AI Platform. The offering combines compute and storage to cut infrastructure overhead and remove the ETL pipelines traditionally needed when merging operational data with analytics. KaBuM! cited it as a low-latency memory layer for its conversational AI agents. It is available across Google Cloud regions from launch, with no infrastructure or pipelines to manage.},
items.title: Databricks Makes Lakebase Postgres Generally Available on Google Cloud

items.summary: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus is reportedly advancing household robot development, with the first product possibly being an autonomous home robot that supports FaceTime calls and controls lights. People who worked on Apple’s robotic projects told The Information it could be named HomeView Ultra, code-named J595, priced at $1,000 or more by 2027—though delays may push the launch to 2028. Critics note its reported features seem underwhelming versus existing smart home devices.
items.title: Apple’s New CEO Pushes a $1,000 Home Robot Targeting 2027

items.summary: PIB Fact Check has labelled a widely shared message as fake, clarifying that the Reserve Bank of India issued no announcement warning of a shortage of Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 50 notes ahead of Diwali. The viral circular, dated October 27, 2026, claimed inadequate supply during the festive season and urged people to use UPI, cards and net banking instead of cash. It also suggested printing was being reduced as part of a less-cash economy move. After the message circulated on WhatsApp, PIB shared its clarification on X, urging people to verify information against official RBI announcements before believing or sharing such messages.
items.title: Press Information Bureau Fact Check Debunks Viral Fake RBI Circular on Small-Denomination Notes

items.summary: Last week Anthropic introduced a system prompt to stop its Claude models from recreating specific existing video games. The change, spotted by user chasm and verified by XDA in binary version 2.1.314 released October 30, allows original or genre games but bars exact reproductions. Engineer Addy Osmani confirmed the addition on social media.
items.title: Anthropic's Claude rules may not curb AI game copying wave

items.summary: The MIT Energy Initiative held its annual research conference on Sept. 22-23 under the theme “Transitioning energy at a pivotal moment,” drawing more than 200 attendees in person and online. Paula Hammond of the MIT School of Engineering opened with remarks stressing an interdisciplinary approach to decarbonization, while keynote speaker Eric Toone of Breakthrough Energy argued that prosperity now depends on cutting emissions. Sessions covered nuclear revival, carbon utilization, startup commercialization, early-stage research, quantum computing at Quantum@MIT led by Danna Freedman, and the energy demands of AI data centers. Steve Clemmer cited an analysis showing hyperscale facilities could be 10 to even 10,000 times larger than a decade ago, raising costs and climate damages; Larry Susskind urged developers to earn community trust through benefits agreements.
items.title: MIT Energy Initiative Conference Explores Decarbonization, AI and Quantum

items.summary: German news magazine Der Spiegel reported that Apple sent spyware threat warnings to members of a delegation accompanying Chancellor Friedrich Merz on his recent trip to Singapore, Japan and South Korea. The alerts reached ministry staff and journalists as well. Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said the federal government is taking the incident very seriously while authorities investigate possible device compromise.
items.title: Apple Warns German Officials of Possible Spyware Breach After Merz Asia Trip

items.summary: Anthropic reported a more than 1,100 per cent surge in quarterly revenue as it prepares for its Wall Street listing later this month. Third-quarter revenue reached US$17 billion, up from US$1.4 billion a year earlier. The company's amended filing showed net loss of US$23.3 billion, mostly from non-cash accounting charges tied to rising valuation, and an operating loss of US$567 million as it paid more for computing capacity.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Revenue Surge Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet began selling €6 billion ($6.7 billion) of bonds on Monday, according to a memo from one deal's managers, testing investor appetite after AI-related doubts triggered tech selloffs and its worst-ever share drop last Thursday. The offering spans seven tranches with demand just over €17 billion; proceeds may repay debt as the company expects up to $205 billion in annual capital spending.
items.title: Alphabet Opens €6 Billion Bond Sale Amid Tech Debt Concerns

items.summary:
Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE malware botnet of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes that Google says its manufacturer intentionally infected to generate revenue through cybercrime. The company attributes the infection with high confidence to Chinese maker Videostrong Technology Co, accusing it of installing a persistent backdoor into device firmware and selling access to criminal affiliates used for ad fraud, residential proxies, and other malware. Google terminated its relationship with Videostrong, revoked its license to manufacture certified Android devices, and banned future affiliates from producing them. Synthient traced the malware after finding it preinstalled on a MECOOL box purchased in late 2025. Although operations were disrupted, the backdoor remains on infected devices unless clean firmware is installed or they are disconnected online.

visual null
items.title: Google Takedowns Million-Device XCPE Android Botnet, Bans TV Box Maker

items.summary: ZDNET reports that OpenAI will merge the chat and work tabs of its ChatGPT desktop app starting in December 2025, according to a note on OpenAI's website. The integrated experience will be tested with select users before wider rollout, which OpenAI says should not disrupt most customers' usage resets or workflows.
items.title: OpenAI Merges ChatGPT Chat and Work Tabs in December
